text: Her pets make an appearance in examples, despite it being an Asynchronous online class she makes time for a review session each week where she goes above and beyond to answer questions and ensure her students understand concepts, doesn't go to quickly, posts content at the start of every week, and grades really fast

This is the worst professor I've had in my time in college. Considering that this was an online class, she completely relied on MyMathLab for all the teaching material, she never did any videos of herself explaining the concepts. When you email her with questions she is ambiguous and is also hard to reach, and grading in her class is too confusing.

Someone forgot to tell her that this class was Intro to Literature. Not intro to poetry. She is clearly a poetry fan and if you dislike a poem she likes she will give you an attitude and mark you down. 90% of the material was poetry. She flat-out told me not to email her again. Got an A but hated every moment and every interaction with this woman

He gives too much work for an online class, 6-7 assignments are all due on Sunday. It should be 2-3 assignments a week, which is enough. Also, don't buy the textbook like I did, he posts everything on Canvas from the textbook, which would have been helpful to know.

The entire class was made up of 3 discussion board posts, a midterm, and a final. Posts were super easy and all the answers to the midterm/final were online so it was the easiest A i have ever received. Ill be honest, I felt like I learned absolutely nothing but an A is an A !

I loved her! She was very supportive of all of us, gave great feedback on our papers, and got us through a very difficult semester by inspiring all of us! She was very encouraging and told us all multiple times that she knew we could handle it! She genuinely cares about her students and helping them succeed! She pushes you to reach your potential.
Open book, fair workload, you'll be fine. E class for a self-disciplined student. as

I took ENTR211 with Laura and it was one of the best classes that I have taken at this University. She is an interesting person, but also genuinely cares about her students doing well. The course offers an A bundle, B bundle, and C bundle, so you essentially pick what grade you want to receive at the end of the Semester. No quizzes, just stories.

Nothing much to be said about her. She is a good person, although it was hard to be learning from 2 different professors at same time especially since professor Natalia Tkachov has very strong and distinct accent in the way she speaks lots of Spanish words which makes it confusing. 

Morevoer, it is the class that needs a lot of changes to be made.

I took Dr. Elliss citizenship class. Dr. Ellis is very passionate about sustainability. Dr. Ellis gives a sufficient amount of assignments, but they help develop essential skills, which I use in other classes at Longwood. He also challenges his students to think differently about sustainable issues.

He will have you work a group of many even though a traditional on line class.
I didnt think I was going to liek this class - he doesnt get back.
BUT the class was pretty decent. Learned soem good things and he grades slow but Good.

A fine professor; lots of easy quizzes and assignments. Fair grader, lectures/module summaries have everything you need, and the information provided makes sense. Great for Running Start students, maybe lacking in direct intellectual stimulation or challenges. Very hands-off.

I had Mrs. Diggs for reading learning support. we worked on Pearson lab the majority of time and had quizzes over Henrietta Lacks's book. that is basically all we did in the class. it should be an easy A as long as you do Pearson, attend class, do quizzes, and do everything she ask toy to.

Prof. Darby was responsive and kind via text--this was an online class. The book was great. Affordable. The quizzes and format were great. The videos were excellent, interesting, and well-done. I really appreciated this class and am signing up for another of hers. She is organized and had good pacing of the material.

There are a lot of experiments and I highly recommend new students to use the 10 hours of complimentary tutoring available to get the best grade possible and double check the experiment reports. The discussions are a lot of fun and engage the student for in depth learning. It is important to prepare for the tests, quizzes, and homework assignments
She is so sweet and good at lectures. Super easy, fun topic. Seems like a lot of work but I barely spent an hour a week on this class.

The professor is very informative on assignments and due dates. I thought I would love this class, but it ended up being one of my least favorite ones and I'm not sure if that's because of the material, or the assignments. It just didn't interest me. But the professor is really passionate about what he does which is cool to see.
Amazing professor, dont have to worry about difficulty. She cares about your grades and is extremely fair. Take her for abnormal psych if possible

Professor Evans has a lot of good stories to tell about the career experiences she's had. I learned a lot about event planning in this class and it helpped me to get an overview of the future career that I would like.

Great professor to take intro to sociology. During the summer term, you have 3 essays which are pretty straight forward if you read the text, as is the case with your weekly quizzes. If you have questions she is available to schedule in office hours, along with TAs. Great class and a breath of fresh air from heavy math/science in engineering.

Cheryl is a great instructor who puts in an effort with every class. She wants her students to do well and you can tell that she isn't just there for a paycheck. I wish I had her in more of my classes.

His group project requires you to write a 20+ page business plan yet he clearly only skims them when it comes to grading, all his critiques were about things that "weren't covered" yet were in the report. This class isn't hard but his expectations are super unclear and his feedback very confusing and frustrating.

Not a hard professor at all. Very clear in grading criteria, usually gives lectures with occasional group activities, and requires little to no textbook usage. Also not a hard grader who gives good feedback.
He is an amazing human being with lots of insights!
He gave a lot of work. Was lenient with the deadlines and cared about the students. Overall not a bad professor, recommend taking him if the class is online.

the last homework is worth 60% of your grade so if you do bad on it you fail no matter how you did on the other projects. the last project is on calculus and physics, but this is an intro class which is supposed to be taken before those classes.

AMAZING is all I can say. Sarah has been one of my favorite nursing professors ever! She really is so passionate about what she does and it comes across in her teaching. She gives you everything that you need to be successful plus she gives a lot of extra credit opportunities. Go to class take notes and study her PP's and you will do good!

Professor Kim makes sure students understand what's going on in class. He's very detailed with labs and makes sure that you're doing the correct steps. He has been extremely willing to work with students. He has also stayed behind to help with understanding material. Quiz almost every week. He exempts 1 assignment and quiz.

I just finished taking her Assembly Language course and never have I ever been in a harder to follow class. Her accent is ridiculously difficult to understand. She grades insanely harshly. Her exams and quizzes never have anything to do with what we studied. Whenever I met with her, you could not speak as she would constantly talk over you. Avoid!!

This professor was in particular hard to read. I think it was his first year, but his teaching style was quick and all over the place. He took feedback from students and it was obvious he was trying to fix himself. His assesment grading was tough. Lots of PDFs and readings that were in quizzes and tests. if you do get him, he willtryhisbesttopass u

ATTENDANCE!! Class was super boring but easy. Only graded by 2 online quizzes, midterm paper (4 pages), and a final exam. Group project got cancelled due to COVID but he made it extra credit. Attendance will destroy your grade. Every class missed will affect your grade. Worth 100 points, wont help your grade only hurts it big time. Very bad policy

Dr. Heinrich was so engaging to have as an in-person teacher, but unfortunately I took this class on zoom. Prerecorded lectures made it really hard to learn, and material wasn't codified across discussion sections, making my section feel behind. There was a lot of great material, but it was unclear what we should've been retaining.

This is one of those classes that will keep you up at night. Loads of HW and the amount of time given on exams is insane, you have to rush on each problem just so you have enough time to take pictures of every question and upload them into the correct box. If you have other options to take this class, please pick one of those you'll thank me later.

Grading criteria is vague and assignment instructions are not clear. She does not provide helpful feedback and lectures are PowerPoint slide after PowerPoint slide of useless text. Not engaging at all, avoid if you can.

There are assignments every day, mostly articles to read and annotate that feel pointless. She never gives clear instructions or guidelines for essays. EVER. She makes every essay you write feel like its not good enough and her "constructive criticism" is not constructive at all just criticism. Do not take this course its mentally draining.

His class was basically listening to lectures and then take 7 exams. His powerpoints weren't very clear and you would often miss critical information for the exam. The exams consist of multiple choices where you just have to memorize names of enzymes and mechanism. It's a class that test your memory not intelligence.

Gia knew her stuff and she always clarified if I had questions. She was there during office hours, and emailed really quickly if I needed anything. Understanding and really took the time out to help me. Thank you!
Will keep you the entire time just out of spite.

She is the worst professor Ive ever had. She never grades anything that Canvas doesnt grade for her. She didnt post the second half of the course until two weeks before the semester was over. I emailed her a few times and still have not heard anything. She is never accessible.
Too smart to be teaching. He is a horrible professor. Can't communicate with someone who doesn't have a pHD.
worst professor ever. very rude and makes snarky comments

PLEASE DONT TAKE HIM. I heard that this is his first year at ramapo. The professor who taught this last year was amazing and she retired sadly. He grades about 5-6 things thats it. I was always stressed out going to this class. He calls on you to go the board to do work, he doesnt offer extra help, all he says is "work the exercises in the book".

Taught a class based upon Star Trek. Was required to buy a book (most FYS classes don't. She used the premise of Star Trek to host a class on liberalism and was happy to force her own beliefs upon her students. Most students don't participate, due to the unwillingness to be criticized for personal beliefs, including religion. Frustrating class.
She si not very young and doesnt have teaching experience yet, Tried to see her on her office hours but wasnt helpful at all, I would never take her again.

Greene is a hilarious guy and I really enjoyed the class. It was super interesting and I really feel like I gained a lot from it. He tells us what we were expected to know for the midterm and final (those are the only tests), and there was one easy paper on a topic of our choosing and 7 short reading responses due by the end of the semester.
Horrible! His course is very tough to pass. Exams are impossible. Don't be fooled by the ratings.

Dr. Lou clearly has a strong understanding of statistics herself, but struggles to communicate that understanding to students. Her lecture slides are poorly structured, she makes many errors while teaching, and she appears very disorganized. There are a variety of better professors for STAT 203 at LUC, I would recommend taking them if possible.

She straight up doesn't know what she's talking about. She reads directly from the powerpoint and doesn't pronounce half the names correctly. She never responds to emails. After a lecture she said "This is on the test but you'll have to look it up cause this is just my opinion". She is also always late, but docs you if you are.
lack of consideration in time for online quizzing, lack of empathy for time

Interesting course, not recommended if you already have a heavy course load. Far more work than a typical 3 credit 100 level course. Expect 2-5 online lectures per week paired with a weekly quiz, HW, discussion, lab and reports. The material isn't difficult, there's just a lot of it and often feels disorganized. Professor is passionate & talks FAST

Ms. Alexia is the best teacher I have ever had! I have never gotten an A in a math class before. She is so good at teaching and answering questions. The longest I have waited for a response through email was a day. She is so nice and genuinely cares. I had her for a semester in person and a semester online. even online, she made a HUGE effort.10/10

He makes you feel bad about not knowing the material. He doesn't curve tests even when class averages are super low. His lectures are often pretty boring, and he carries an arrogant persona throughout the entire semester. It feels as if he finds enjoyment when his students don't do well. He doesn't tell you anything about what will be on the tests.

I'll spare you my complaints, seems like this course is inevitable for SOM students. Be on time for every single one of the assignment, start ahead that is how you will have time to complete these assignments. Find good teammates and it goes a long way, textbook material is only important for exams. Manage your time and you should be fine.

Her assignments are very helpful for studying and understanding the material. I like the mix of writing discussion questions and textbook questions and practice quizzes and exams she provides for us. I also like how she keeps us engaged in learning. She's really nice.

Jess is very smart but she gives very hard tests. I recommend studying the calculations more because she focuses more on those. Do her practice problems please, it will help you during midterms and finals. Try not to do notes during her lecture, do them outside of class because she talks very fast so try to pay attention.
she was decent. tough grader and her assignments were hard to comprehend at times tbh. she was nice and all but her class was boring.

Cheng is a kind human, but he is simply not a good teacher. His lectures were extremely unorganized, confusing and rushed. He sets you up to memorize the content, not understand it. Practice exams/study guides are NOTHING like the tests. I think STOR 155 is intended to be an easy class, but he made it way more difficult than it should be.

I love Dr. Ajaj, but his lectures were so boring and you need to be there since attendance is such a big part of your grade. All tests and quizzes were taken in class, but were open book. At the end of the semester, there was a 4-6 page paper, but it was very manageable. I recommend taking this class for a science gened, but only if you don't skip.

I had Professor Wagner for film 100 as well and loved him! He gives great feedback on his scripts in person and makes sure that his students participate in critiques. I wish he would justify his grading... sometimes it isn't quite clear what he is looking for overall when you submit. But I think he has great ideas and solutions and really cares!
Loved 101A with Prof Carodenuto! She was amazing and I am pretty sure I aced the final.

Pretty easy. You don't have to buy a textbook, he provides it for you. Read chapter, take quiz, forum, and respond to 2 ppl is weekly hw. I took the summer course so it was really short. Provides good feedback. Makes sure you understand. You have a chance to retake quiz 3 times
David is a great professor. He really cares for his students and their success.

Enjoyed his class, but grading is absurd. On an assessment, he argued that if he gave his colleagues my essay to grade, they would have graded it lower. He also took points off for the same mistake twice & took additional points off of HIS inferences of my writing & "necessary" things he never told the class. Nice but wildly inconsistent grading

His lectures are interesting, but you need to attend every class possible since he does not post the PowerPoints. This online course has weekly quizzes and writing assignments every two weeks that are fairly easy. The quizzes are open notes however the final and midterm are not. He gives extra credit for attendance when the class is fairly empty.

I took wall for Fall 2019 Math 27. It's pretty obvious he's a beginning teacher. His lectures were all over the place and many times he even confused himself with what he was trying to do. He had lots of little group projects that weren't really beneficial to the class and was overall a really difficult teacher to try and learn from.

Very smart woman. . . sometimes too smart for her own good, but hey she made the class interesting. The exams are easy, that is if you study the vocabulary she gives you before the midterm and final. The paper due during the semester is doable, but be prepared to put in a lot of work for it, and the final paper is a pain in the butt (but doable).
I took gen bio 1 lab with her and really liked her. She is super friendly and is accessible outside of class. She wants her students to succeed and gives good advice.

Disoganized and didn't use Canvas well. Emailed slides at last minute then updated version posted on campus. Some slide sets had dates, some didn't, and no file naming convention to help the student make sure they had all the updated versions. Often vague/evasive when answering questions. Lectures pretty good. Breakouts I didn't add to class

Imagine the most average college professor in your mind right now. This is Prof. Iaconis. The work is pretty average, I'm just lazy and got a C+. He has a very monotone voice that might put you to sleep but he has occasional jokes that are pretty funny. He lets class go early a lot of days and he is in no way a bad choice to have as a prof.

Make sure you know how to learn from a math textbook. Professor Drenska seems to be a very caring lady, but she does not know how to teach. She copies proofs and examples directly out of the book, without any explanations. Your TA will teach you much more. The homework assignments are very manageable and are included in your grade.

The class was adjusted to be half asynchronous and synchronous due to COVID. I liked setting my own schedule to watch the lectures then going to class to work with other students. The professor is nice and caring, just do the work and study for all the exams.
Gives packets of homework due the next day

Can't recommend this guy enough, remarkable individual. Does a fantastic job of incorporating students into discussions and really gets you engaged with what he's teaching. Very caring person, wants you to succeed while still challenging you. Attendance is tough but fair and he's super accessible outside of class.

I don't go to PCC, I'm taking this class because I thought it would be easier at community college. I WAS WRONG. Way too much work and unnecessary policies. First homework due 2 days after class start, you need the $100 textbook to do the homework. Takes 5+ days to ship. No late submission policy. Good thing she's not a math professor.

Def need to do the reading for the lectures. Prof encourages a lot of participation and the classes are very discussion heavy. Graded on 2 take home exams (short answer and essay) and 2 forum posts. Prof grades a little tough on exams. Taking notes during class will help for the exams. Overall very nice, helpful, and understanding prof.

lectures are completely useless as they are nothing similar to homework nor tests. also, lecture videos are entirely vague and does not explain the process for any example, she just does it with zero connection to what was learned

He never graded your work, hell grade up until the middle of the quarter then stop, hell also never respond to your questions so you cant get the help you need, it was really difficult to tasks his class.

Professor Bednar is hard to call a professor. The class content each week consisted of a video, podcast and reading. Both the podcast and video were never shorter than 1 hour of just straight yapping. And to add to that fire, they were all old recycled videos from the covid days. The readings were egregious and the evals were just summaries.
The teacher seems to have wide knowledge of marketing, but the classes are so quick that we can not have te time to process and absorbe too much information.

He does not cover any material in class, just posts a PowerPoint that you are expected to review before class for the in class quiz. Extremely disorganized and often does not post material in a time for students to review. The TAs did most of the actual teaching in this class.

Very nit picky about what she wants in her papers. Nice person, very liberal, mediocre professor though. She had a us read two books in her class. I got a decent grade without even reading them and relied on spark-note type websites. Ethnography at the end of the class was pretty easy though.

First and foremost, Dr. Reed is one of the nicest and relatable professors I've had. Very nice guy overall. Although he's a great guy, I struggled to comprehend some of his calculus explanations. I took calculus in high school, but still felt kind of puzzled on some of the topics he taught. I wished he did more example problems in class.

Rita Persaud has been teaching and educating students at George Brown College for the past 4+ years. During that time, students have learned about her husband, her daughter, her many many many accolades, her business connections, and her overall super duper awesome life and career. Students have not learned the course content however. You get it?

She cares about her students but she is super tough grader. I have never seen a professor who grades super toughly for writing on classmates' posts. When we comment on our classmates, most professors give full marks but this professor DOES NOT..... super tough grader

Bonnie is a lovely woman and will go the extra mile to make sure you succeed, both in her class and the future. She can be a little disorganized, but in all fairness this was the first time the class ever ran. I didn't feel like I learned that much, it was just a standard foundation course.

He does not care about you as a student at all, He says "Email me if you have any issues" I email him and he tells me to figure the things out myself. when clearly I tried to do so and failed. He thinks you're stupid if you start reaching out for help. Just an overall a horrible teacher I would not recommend.
Shes very nice and really understanding

Honestly if you don't get an A in this class that's on you. I hate math and have never received an A before always just C or F's but this professor is really caring! Easiest math class he even gives you the answers you just got to show the work . There's a project he walks you through every single step. The test can made up.
Gives excellent feed back on graded material. Lectures are given in a easy to follow manner and will patiently go over material again if you did not get the concept the first time.

CS486 - Virtual Reality
----------------------
The class says Monday 9:30-12:00, but it is not.. You have to go every single Friday or else you won't finish any of the homework required in the class. She is also biased and grades you by how much she likes your project. If you are just trying to get by, aka DOING AN ELECTIVE, do not take this class.

Dr Nash is okay at best. His lectures and directions are vague. Repetitive HW but easy assignments. Gets angry at students when they don't know an answer, gives good feedback and easy to reach out. Doesn't cover most of the readings he just uses videos so brace yourself for the midterm,dont sleep on the reading, recommend other proffessor,

Dr. Hale is incredibly kind, and is one of the most engaging lecturers I've ever had. I've had him for two classes and enjoyed them both- would definitely recommend him for anyone with a genuine interest in linguistics

I was often so confused in class. She made everything political as well. I couldn't dare say my opinion because I know I would get a bad grade. I wish she could put these ratings into consideration. She is nice, sometimes, but this class just feels like a routine to her, and she doesn't actually care. I couldn't name 5 important things I learned.
Solid professor overall, classes are participation heavy but if you made mistakes it was never met with harsh criticism. Would definitely recommend for a first time French student.

Trust me! Go to office hours if you're having a difficult time understanding the material, he's so helpful. For exams, you're able to use a 5x5 index card as a "cheat sheet" front and back which was definitely helpful. The final exam is a full sheet. Quizzes are open note. Overall, you should be fine if you keep up with the syllabus.

Good professor, but speaks in a very low tone that is sometimes very hard to hear. Sometimes I would miss things during the lectures because I genuinely could not hear her. But other than that I had no issues

Worst teacher I have ever experienced in my 30 years of life. Lectures are 3-5 minutes long and are not useful whatsoever. She teaches no concepts and expects you to teach yourself by "practicing". Denise is a slap in the face to BCITs integrity, and I feel like I was scammed out of $800 in a disgusting way even though I managed to get an A somehow

Hes awesome! i took him for 211 &313. Both classes aren't easy subjects, but the way he formats his class allows you to learn and do well. No exams! Assessments are on his lecture material. Don't take the class if you want an A just to be handed to you tho, u have to work hard but its so doable! Ppl complain because they don't want to put in effort

Exams are heavily weighted but she gives a generous curve. Lectures are just reading off of a power point so you just have to teach yourself. Do the dynamic study modules to help solidify your knowledge of the material but don't depend on them. Try to read the power points before class so you can follow the lecture better. Utilize online resources.

The material is not hard but she makes it hard and extremely confusing. The instructions to assignments contradict the syllabus and her announcements. Her feedback is most of the time only "you got the incorrect answer" which is not helpful. She has absolutely no sympathy for student situations. Her class on D2L is so unorganized and a whole mess.

Took this course based entirely on these reviews and now I'm VERY sorry that I did. First and foremost, his lectures are INCREDIBLY long, boring, and DO NOT even cover all of the material on his exams! You are left completely on your own in this course for answers. There is also NO EXTRA CREDIT either! Trust me, do not walk, RUN away from this guy!

Get ready to read...a lot. Also, there are a few papers throughout the semester & then a final paper at the end. He's a very tough grader. I would recommend that if you're not a history major, don't take this class - it is rigorous. If you do take this class, go to the writing center sometimes for help. Also, attendance is strict. Plan accordingly.

Very lackadaisical class. Many people didn't show up until speech days and passed. He talks a lot about his past and outside life so class gets off topic quickly. However, he does get very upset if the class isn't paying attention during someones speech. It counts against you if you sign up for a speech day and aren't ready. Lots of extra credit

Great professor, understood personal situations happen and tries to work with you to help you get the best grade possible. One quiz a week about the chapter, easy 12 questions. Super caring, 100% would recommend

This was one class that taught me skills I actually use in other classes and outside of school which is cool. The quizzes are really tough, so study slides and homework videos hard (actually watch and read stuff)- and take notes. For the final, find patterns in sensors and you will be ok. The TA is a live savor for homework to guarantee an A.

He is the best nursing faculty in the department!! Very enthusiastic and passionate about teaching us. What I really like about him is he never makes you feel stupid when you ask a question.  If you have him, you are in it for lots of learning.

Dr. Wilson was always super nice in lab and always helped if we had questions. I had no problems in her lab the entire semester. As long as you go to lab, pay attention, and turn things in on time, an easy A.
She s very smart, very good teacher.

Class was good overall. His way of teaching is a little dry, but it could just be his voice (monotone). Of course there are papers, along with other assignments. Group collaboration as well. Did not ever need to open the textbook. Approachable, but can sometimes come off as being harsh. Class was okay, just not the best. Different teaching style.

I took his College Success Skills my first semester and it was honestly extremely helpful. He helps answer a lot of questions you have about college and you will use everything you learn. None of the information he gives goes to waste. Trust me, you'll be thankful you took his class.

I can go the entire semester without coming to his lecture I'll still be fine cause he just reads off slides. The midterm was brutal, and he did not prepare us well for the exam. I suggest everyone take this class last semester of college, so if you don't do as well, GPA won't really matter at that point

Dr. Elenkov is an added value to Marist College community. He is an academic seamaster; his expertise in explaining some of the most difficult concepts in the current business arena faced by the global soc, made the subject extremely easy to place in perspective. Foreshadowing, his lectures align perfectly with practial global bus. operations.

I don't know where to start. If you don't need this class don't take it. If you do, take it with someone else. There's a TON of homework and she's not good at clarifying what she wants out of it. The group projects are last-minute and too much. In class, She has said "If you want to work on the project, you may"  so basically just do something else

Do not take this professor. She gives tests every class. Overloads you with work and things to study for the next test (every 2 days). Very crazy lady. Makes you "rate" yourself in front of the class. Terrible class !!

This was my first class with Broward College, I am a dual enrolled high school senior. I was taking two dual classes at the same time, so my reason for why I appreciated Dr. Perez are as follows: She spaces her work out very well, follows the same pattern so nothing takes you surprise. Very understanding if you are busy and gives genuine feedback!

OConnor has you do 2 article reviews based on the article she has you read & wont allow you to do any outside sources for those at all. Also, you have to do an Essay and will randomly assign you a topic, check your e-mail for it. Lots of readings on revel, quizzes and weekly short assignments too. Great teacher!
Dislike

She is a nice person, HOWEVER DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS. She teaches way too fast, her tests are ridiculously long and she reviews the day OF the test. On the day of exam she always lectures before the test and its a waste of time because you're rushing to finish 110-125 question exams. Her study guides are vague, lectures are boring, DONT TAKE HER.
Accounting's tough but she lays it out in a good way. Tests are fair and homeworks are helpful. Just have to put the work in

She is very young so she understands how stressful life is as a college student. She is very caring and respectful. She responds to your emails as soon as possible, even if it's at 3AM. The transition to online classes bc of COVID19 was difficult and she understood that. She was very fair with grading, however, she does take long to finish grading.
I had troubles but she was always available. She even made a class program in advanced just for me, because I took 113 2 years ago. She use too much Spanish in class.

This class is basically the biology of Civil Engineering - all memorization with boring lectures that make it hard to stay focused. Ferron's extra credit assignments are a huge grade booster at the end of the semester, but that's only to counter how she hurts the class by giving extremely difficult exams and throwing out random pop quizzes.

I thought he was a pretty average teacher, nothing special. He would help you if you went after class or to office hours, but other than that in lectures I learned almost nothing. I had to rely on myself reading the book and powerpoints to learn the material. The in class quizzes sucked and I did bad on most, but aced all the big tests.
He is fine, he is very slow and has a soft voice. Sometimes he just gets off topic and starts doing complicated things but its a good class overall.
Just keep up with the work and you'll be fine. Nothing too crazy with work load.

The class is redundant, but Anzyl herself is a caring person. Except for the journals, you should be able to get an A or B on most assignments. There is more to this class than it seems, though, so remember to do the work, as not doing so can set you back. She will understand if you get sick and miss out as well, just let her know ahead of time.

She doesn't care about undergrads at all and is so focused on her own research. Her lecture videos were so boring, and she basically read the slides. Her exam was T/F on super minor points. Really? It's just lazy to give a T/F exam in college. I went to her OH and she was incredibly unhelpful. I regret taking this course with her.

Awful Professor. zero flexibility for in-class attendance (funerals? too bad, losing credit). No clear explanation for answers to quizzes beyond "You should know this, I taught you this in my lecture." 

Clearly an ineffective professor, yet an accomplished academic. Be prepared to devote significant time to coursework.

Getting homework every week and not getting feedback on how to improve made me dread thinking about the class. Professor Vlad is nice and is very skilled at charcoal, but the heavy workload and how he taught drawing techniques became extremely draining. Lots of work to do. Reading responses are tough

This class is a breeze for someone who has participated in theatre before. For people who haven't, this class might be a bit of a challenge. You are forced out of your comfort zone. Professor Johnston is an amazing professor, very passionate about history and humorous at times. Just make sure to do her identifications, they really bring your grade down even if you get A's & B's on her exams. She's also pretty hot too.

Professor Cash is AMAZING! Loved her class so much, I'm taking another! She is passionate about history and truly cares about her students' success in the course. 1 midterm, exit tickets for attendance, 2 papers, final exam consisted of 9 slides. My favorite teacher ever! Always enthusiastic about her job, gave really good lectures, and always went above and beyond to make sure her students understood the material. A good teacher, but the subject is challenging, and you have to study or take really good notes. He is the worst professor I have ever had. He may have a PhD in Marketing, but clearly wants to be an English professor. He takes off points for APA formatting that is accurate. All he cares about is grammar and writing style. I even had my paper reviewed by a professional, and Hansen still told me it was wrong. Switch professors if you can!
I promise you there are better professors out there this one should be your last option!!!

This class is challenging overall but this professor does help a little. The "notetakers" she provides help with taking notes but reading and studying on your own is necessary. Exams are 60% of the grad so good luck.

Very nice fair professor. Made the summer class nice and quick and in my opinion was good at explaining the material. If things were ever confusing he was happy to go back and re-explain as many times as needed. Labs were a little confusing on what was expected for prelabs and conclusions but other than that I would recommend this professor.
Dr. Hart is a great story teller and has lots of real life experience to share about special education.

Encourages bad medical practice. Insisted that students should ASSUME a women took an at home pregnancy test, that it was negative, and to NOT perform any additional testing. Kenny is very enthusiastic and passionate about philosophy. He gives a lot of extra credit in the form of what he calls "charity." You are not graded on many things. He takes attendance and discussion for a grade, so it is best if you suck it up and participate; it usually pays off at the end. He was not my favorite, but he does want you to succeed

Dr. Parkinson is phenomenal! Overall, very caring and knowledgeable.  However, this class is HARD! She is perfectly aware that this course is the notorious "pre-med" weed out class, but sets clear guidelines on how to do well in the course. An "A" is difficult to achieve, but not impossible. Practice exams and book questions are your best friend!

Let me get something clear: I dont like math. I cant stand it and the thought of sitting at a math class makes me feel stressed as hell. Professor Ly made me love math, which was a surprise to me. I loved taking MTH 23 with him, and Im sure you will, too. If youre worried about taking Stats for the very first time, take his class.

Quite possibly the worst prof Ive had at TCNJ. Not only is he unqualified to teach HR management but he is condescending and rude. Lectures consist of the lecture notes from the textbook publisher and he stretches each class to fill the whole time. Wastes time reading lists of things about himself and his son for hours. Do not take his class

Tyler is a very smart guy, when it comes to his topics of interest. He tries his best, but he's impatient with answering questions and sometimes it just seemed like he thought we were all idiots. Questioned classmates as well as my own intelligence, more respect would have been nice.

Professor Kabre's class was very easy, and she provided good feedback. However, sometimes if you asked a question in class, she would explain the answer in the most difficult way possible. She is a sweet person, but her teaching skills aren't that good. If possible, I would avoid her class but at the same time she isn't a bad teacher.

Professor Rivest is a total professional. He comes to class prepared and gives engaging lectures. Personal finance isn't the most scintillating subject to teach but he kept my interest and provided me with a lot of wisdom. He's an excellent teacher and definitely knows his stuff.

Phenomenal professor! I absolutely loved my time in class. He was a wonderful lecturer, always got his points across very clearly while keeping everyone engaged. His passion for the subject always shone through and I loved it. I walked into the class not knowing much about sociology and walked out with a minor in sociology. Take him if you can!

The course was not difficult but it was unique. The professor lacks in communicating, only sent two class-wide emails entire semester. And her response times vary from minutes to days. I personally withdrew bc mental health caused me to slack off which due to her very strict make up/ due dates, prevented me from recovering my grade.

Lectures had nothing to do with anything we were tested on. Feel free to skip. R tutorial attendance is necessary though. He was unwilling to give much help on the homeworks and admitted to not answering every email he gets from students- he will ignore you. Ask lots of questions anyways to see what you can get out of him. Start hw early.
She is a tough grader. So many papers and limited time. Her feedbacks are not very clear. I would not recommend anyone to take her class.
Prof Betchart isn't a bad guy; however, he tends to over explain. He is very accessible. The textbook is your homework. The tests are very similar to the homework.

Although I did well in Fitness and Physical Activity and Professor Kleis is a nice guy, it was too much effort just for the core requirement. We learned complex info about bioenergetics, nutrition, and exercise planning that I'll never use again. Also, all we really do is go over PowerPoints, so if you want to do well get ready to cram!
A lovely professor, and pretty good considered this is her first time teaching. A little dry at times but that is a given since she is new. She will become a great professor someday!

Professor Thompson is a great teacher and I learned a lot from her Negotiations class, however, this was easily one of the hardest classes I have ever taken. The grading is very difficult and there are very few assignments. Make sure to read the chapters VERY WELL and take lots of notes (quizzes are very hard). Participation is also a must.

He was horrible. The tests had random questions that were not taught and were graded super hard. He only taught irl and did not post anything online or use anything online like a PowerPoint. He does not explain and teaches by writing equations on the board and not explaining anything at all.

Burdock is such a great film professor. His enthusiasm and knowledge of film made this my favorite class. In class discussions are low key and easy to participate in. Its the same homework every week so there's no surprises when it comes to assignments. It can take a bit to get papers back because he genuinely enjoys what his students have to say.
This class can be difficult to understand. So hee does work with students who come to office hours so that does help. Tough grader and very hard to get an A.

A history of math class should not be that hard. When I search teaching videos on Youtube, teachers give examples of how to change old time notions into modern ones. Ramesh is a caring lecturer and goes out of his way to help students. Alas, his lectures are dry, with mostly him reading slides. Tests and homework make little sense. I asked a friend who works in networking and he thought the content was out of date and sometimes inaccurate.

This course was great for students in the Homeland Security world. This was by far my favorite course to date at Embry-Riddle. Dr. Aydiner is an outstanding instructor. He was very helpful and provided quick and easily comprehensible responses to all questions. I wish all instructors were as understanding as he is.

Dr. Lauster was great. When asking for help the only thing that fell through was the amount of time it took for a response but when you get one he's thorough on how to help you with whatever it is. He's a nice guy, very lecture heavy but if you pay attention the information is there.

Pray for a good TA. If you get a chill one, you can BS the answers. Otherwise, the homework is unnecessarily confusing, the lab sucks, but RAQs are free. 1511L was much easier than 1510L, and we could leave much earlier. Good luck.

Anthony is a great professor he tries his best to incorporate students into his lecture and actually has visual notes, unlike many professors. He did have a lot of group projects that I did not like. Other than that his workload was very manageable and reading the textbook was not the worst. We did have to purchase a textbook for this class.

No clear instructions for assignments. Loves to plan/cancel zooms with very little notice. Also loves to give 0 feedback on assignments. Will say she is available for outside help & questions but really is not. Always is changing aspects of projects and contradicting herself. Worst class I have ever taken, switch out if you can.

I wouldn't recommend him! 1)I couldn't get a hold of him for almost a month. 2)his test and quiz Q's were so abstract, there was really no point in studying. I actually learned a few things in his class unlike the other 95% of professors. Definitely recommend.

Charles Peak is the bane of my undergrad career. He gives unclear instructions while assuming you know how to do everything. This course is lecture heavy and it's hard to understand because of his heavy accent. I feel like I barely learn anything from these lectures in the class. Your course grades mostly depend on your test scores.

Okay prof but you can tell he's full of himself. Puts a lot of weight on the class so if you're not super passionate about public affairs it might give you the ick. Annoying grading because he focuses so much on writing instead of content. Made us keep cameras on in lecture for attendance, very annoying. It's literally the bottom of all PA classes.

Professor Huang is such a nice man, but just not the best professor. He is very accessible outside of class but very difficult to understand and communicate with. BEH255 is honestly a pointless class, but he made it very difficult. He is accessible outside of class though and will try to help you with questions you might have.

Recommend her completely. Best Professor out there, obviously cares about all her students and pushes you to do the best. As long as you do her work and turn everything in ,youll pass. May God Bless her , we need more professors like her in this world now.
He's a new professor and truly cares about his students! He made this course simple, super easy A!!

She is a very nice professor. All the assignments are written by hand she doesn't care for electronics. There are writing assignments every class night due for the next class. All of your writing assignments are based off of your own thoughts and experiences. It is the easiest class you will ever take.

George is a man of great experience and has a lot to offer. Admittedly, I learned more from his personal stories than the actual course material. Exams are all online, class isnt hard if you read the book. Has great Guest Speakers.

Lectures are boring and hard to follow to understand main ideas. Saddened that learning about a very important topic for freshman students is being taught poorly. Previous semesters and professors made this class an easy A for the ethnic studies requirement. She somehow manages to make even getting an AB difficult.

If you are someone who isn't good at math, Proffesor Risk is the perfect teacher for you. He is so understanding and very flexible. The homework is on Aleks and it isn't hard if you take good notes. While some people didn't seem to love this professor, I had a great experience and learned so much. It really helps to make flashcards leading up to every test as there is a lot of memorization. She is a harsh grader so you need to include all the details on short answer questions. She is also very open to questions in class and out.

He's a pretty fair grader, but that's probably the only good thing I can say. He's SUPER lecture heavy he'll talk at you for the whole 2 hour 40 minute lecture (during which he's basically just reading off of the slides the whole time). Taught myself for all of the homeworks. Term project is a LOT and he gives you super vague requirements.

At the time of this review, I don't have my final grade yet. But I do fear that I will have to retake the class again. I wish Luis taught the class in the spring because he is such a great professor! He was very witty in class and tried his best to pass most of his students.
Best professor I ever had and lets you use a cheat sheet.

She is one of the best CIS Professors ever! She is very nice and she cares about her students. If you have any difficulties or need help with anything, just talk to her, and she would try to help you as much as possible. Her lecture is very simple and clear enough for you to learn the basics of Python. Easy A, so take her and you will love Python.

She's very engaging with students, even at 9 in the morning. She lectures very well and creates an environment where we actually hold conversations and know one another. She's caring and easy to talk to.

Worst professor ever. He does not teach and when you ask him to teach he says we have no time or he will go through it too fast to comprehend. He acts as if everything is a race. Stay away from any of his classes, this is the worst professor I've ever had. HE IS AWFUL. If taking one of his classes be ready to teach yourself cause he will not.
He is the worst professor I have ever had. Don't take him.
i wish she was my mom. very understanding, caring, engaging, and taught about more than just linguistics.

honestly a great guy but not the best lecturer. there are online quizzes almost every week which are very very useful for the exams. Syllabus schedule was not accurate as he would forget when midterm were. very flexible with hw due dates tho.

Shes a smart person but not a good teacher. Very disorganized and gives too much homework assignments. She expects anybody who takes any of her classes to be on the same page as her so do yourself a favor and avoid her at all costs

Kellie was overall a fine teacher. She didn't really try to be relatable to the class which was frustrating. There are 2 exams for the class that are based off the textbook.
One of the worst professors you'll ever take. She thinks a 101 level course is a 400 level. Assigned an entire book a week before it was due and grades papers like its an upper-level English class.

Can't teach, focuses more on the beginning class than the intermed one. I had her for the split class. Doesn't know how to multi task. Most class I sat on the computer doing other work. It's an easy class, just boring and most class don't need to show up because there's nothing to do. Won't learn any new skills.

Professor Aranda is okay; he is from Spain and speaks English decently, but whenever you have a question he has a hard time understanding what you're confused about, so overall it's a little hard to learn from him. He just has very high expectations; I wouldn't call him a naturally good professor but he wants you to do well, and is funny sometimes.

Professor Wood was my favorite writing teacher!!! He's very caring for his students and makes the effort to give help that they need when writing papers. The only thing is sometimes I feel like his lectures were a little dry and lacked structure. But there is clear grading criteria for what your grade is based on, so just focus on papers & u good!

She doesn't take attendance, but you MUST participate in class if you want to succeed. Her lectures are hard and her tests are VERY hard. She isn't the best at explaining in class. Fall2021. He's nice but I wasn't the biggest fan on how weird he was about attendance & participation. I did well on my tests, not so well on participation but my grade pretty much ONLY reflected participation and not my grasp on the material. It's THAT class where the material is easy but they want to make you work for it just because they can.
Very good teacher who gives good instructions and cares for the student's success. Quite a few extra credit opportunities

Super fun and pretty easy class (especially for a first year freshman!) only 2 major tests, along with 2 essays that are easy to write as long as you put in the effort! A genuinely understanding teacher who loves her line of work, definitely a class I do not regret taking!

Professor Gallardo enjoys teaching her classes but isn't super accommodating. She makes up assignments on the spot in class and then takes off points with no explanation. She also isn't very forgiving if you skip class and if you let her know the legitimate reason (sick, emergency, travel...etc.) beforehand.
Dr. Malka is a fantastic lecturer. He uses a lot of detail and his office hours are useful.

took this class during the summer and first she didn't teach 60% of her class, was assigning  6+ hrs of recorded lectures to watch every week along with our 3.5 hrs in class lectures. We didn't get the grades back for our first 2 exams until hrs before the final drop deadline, and also ignored canvas messages when asked about when we get our grades

She's not clear on her instructions for assignments and she changes her mind on the assignments and how she wants them a lot. She tries too hard when she lectures. If you end up taking her class goodluck because she will give you so much homework to the point that your main focus is her class and you won't be able to focus on your other classes.

I had Professor Abood as my clinical instructor in nursing school. At first I thought she was ok, towards the middle of the semester it felt like she was picking on me specifically for things that usually wouldn't matter. I had heard from another student in my class that was being picked on and graded harder than others. Just don't get in her way.
Pretty harsh.
Overall, she grades easily and assigns light homework throughout the semester. I wish she taught a humanities 002 class because I would take her again 100%. It was basically an easy A for me!

David Ryans classes are life changing. You will get 150% more from this class than any other and your writing will improve tremendously. I am so grateful to have had David for a professor. He is the best educator Ive encountered in over five years post-graduate courses.

She is thoughtful, kind, and professional. She expects the very best from students and is understanding of personal/family emergencies. She tackles on so much but still has time to inspire students. I'm always looking forward to her lectures/clinicals. She wants you to succeed, so don't expect a handout. Put in the work and she will notice.

As a guy, Ryan is super nice, however, as a prof was not great. He was all over the place with his lecture material and wasn't super great at explaining or answering questions. Also, the exam for this course was the same as the upper-level course taught by him.

Prof.Lee is a great teacher. If you want a chill/fun class, but also want to actually learn the subject Prof.Lee is for you. One thing I'd point out is her leniency with grading. There were a few assignments that I submitted which were sub-par, yet she gave me a high score on them (that I clearly don't think I deserved). Overall excellent.

He's the department chair as well as a professor. Information was solid. Grading was a bit slow (always on Sunday night, last minute - but that's just like the students!). Course announcements were never updated through the term, but everything else seemed fine.

Tia is a very tough grader for such a simple class. Instructions are often unclear and she does not give you a chance to make up work after giving confusing and poorly written instructions. The assignments and quizzes are extremely easy, but it's very easy to make a simple mistake and receive a low grade in her class.

Professor Holder is the best! He was passionate about teaching and the subject and is willing to work with you. There are weekly news reviews and a few quizzes-TAKE GREAT NOTES and you'll be fine! Miss class and you'll miss important information so make a point to go to class. I would recommend Professor Holder over and over again.

Prof Esteban is an amazing professor and incredibly personable. He moved deadlines multiple times during the semester when students needed more time and was a constant resource. His in-lecture demos are immensely helpful for the projects. He goes above and beyond for his students and genuinely wants to see them succeed.

I was disappointed by the way that Rachel taught this class. She lectures very slowly - some of my high school classes went at a faster pace. She rambles and has big classes do "think pair share" which is just not a good use of our time. I just felt like a lot of my time was wasted in this class. The tests are easy though. Don't buy the book.

Took Ahmed for CS1 and the experience was similar. Did notice there were less overall resources for this class though. Still plenty of EC, a curve (2-3%), very fair tests and quizzes (0 curveballs), he drops lowest quiz and PA, also no lab exam. The PAs in general are much easier and way shorter than his CS1 PAs. Overall great class experience.

If I knew this class was going to be an accelerated stats/SCM/math class, I would have just taken blow-off electives instead of going for this ASU-specific cert. I really loved all other BDA classes but this one. Get ready to use 50 different formulas and have the tests be 70% weighted towards math where if you screw up on #3, 4-17 are wrong.

AVOID AT ALL COST! Thick Indian accent, which makes it very difficult to understand what he is teaching. Class is based on note taking and tests. Attendance is mandatory and expect to participate or he will publicly shame you if you don't know what the answer is. Knowledge of Algebra, Geometry and Pre-calculus is a must to easily follow along!!!

Professor Varman provides excellent lectures which can substitute the book. The topics are well defined and include the equations. The homework and exams are fair and are based on the given material. Extra credit activities are available throughout the course. All in all a consistent and meaningful course.
I enjoyed his lectures and hes hilarious. I feel like if you dont take good notes youll not do well on the tests, but thats true of most classes

quizzes every week, a total of 7 tests through out semester, and all while weekly homework was due every tuesday. making an a/b is possible if you are self disciplined this class is certainly not recommended for anyone who is not willing to put in the necessary work and study time.
Great professor. Highly recommend taking his class.
Dr. Eshete is a very reasonable and knowledgeable prof. Fair with grading, deadlines and replies emails right away. Cool experience!

She's nice but doesn't grade anything on time ... like ever?? She grades a bit harshly too so I'd be careful taking her for a WID class. Class is just discussion based and you have like 5 lengthy articles to read each week :/
Great teacher ����

Eh, he's an okay professor. You will be graded on four tests and the homework. He does not give a clear understanding on what will be on the test and takes a while to grade them. He honestly is not a bad professor, but you have to pay attention or youll fall behind. I cant tell if his sarcasm is funny or not. Final counted for 30% of the final grade. Do well on exams, and youll get an A.

Professor Yaqub is NEVER clear in her instructions. When you ask for clarification because you are confused she either 1)laughs at you and your incompetence or 2)yells at you for asking for clarification. You will never know what you are supposed to do so you often have to guess and hope that your guess is correct and that your grade isn't ruined.
I liked this class .There were reaction papers, quizes, tests and a group project. Does offer extra credit

Worse teacher ever. She does not know how to teach. She just sits there while lecturing and does everything on perjector. She gets upset if you ask her questions or for help. She has test ever 2 chapers. She requires mymathlab and has 3-4 assignment for hw per week. If you miss mathlab hw she does not have make ups. Don't take her!!

Professor King was a really great professor. The class was difficult and there were papers and quizzes but if you do the work you will get the grade you want. Overall, I would take him again, really interesting.

Professor Kim was a very nice teacher, she expects a lot of her students but does not give proper or clear directions and explanations. If you struggle with writing I would not recommend this teacher. When asking for help it is very difficult because she does not respond to emails and leaves mediocre comments on your assignments.

By far worst teacher I've ever had. Literally dodges questions and makes you feel stupid. Never uses real examples without over complicating them with variables and steps. I learned the course on my own with the help of YouTube and the internet.

His lab is very easy ! However, his test are very hard ! They are 40-50 very detailed short answered question. I like lecture classes but his lecture are an overload. Many people got 60% or lower on each test. Nice man but, unnecessarily hard teacher

Not the best teacher for anatomy, her grading scale is higher than other bio5 instructors & she is really vague when you ask her Qs about upcoming exams in the class. Hardly any E/c in the course & she expects you to keep up without giving you a good idea of what the main topics are to focus on. There are Better bio5 teachers at hartnell than her

Dr. Tran-Ba teaches a very difficult session of classes. P. Chem is not easy and succeeding in these classes can be difficult. However, he does greatly care about his student population. He wants nothing but our success, but has very high expectations. He did everything he could during the pandemic for us, and will do so when classes start again.

The accounting mod is incredibly difficult and fast paced, but prof Mukhopadhyay does his best to make sure we understand the content. He's accessible outside of class and really helpful when you ask him questions. Super nice guy.

She read off the PowerPoints and did not give additional information. I ended up teaching myself. She is unapproachable and does not make time to help you. She makes hurtful remarks to her students. Her class of over 85% of the students were failing. She doesnt write her own exams and can not explain the context. Incorrect information on exams.

Strictly avoid! She did not grade half our things for the entire semester until 3 weeks before the course ended. The class wasn't hard but none of us knew if we were passing or failing the course until the very last day

The course is self-taught with TA's available for extra assistance, although the online program makes it easy to understand. He drops your lowest quiz and test grades and gives you all semester to complete the material for 100%, but 70% of the current module must be complete to unlock the quiz/test. Easy to pass just be sure to ask if you need help

This course was super easy and Ryleigh was awesome! Homework was graded on completion, not your actual answers and she dropped the lowest 6 homework grades, 3 quiz grades, and a 1 exam grade. This class is a lot of work but it's online so it's expected. I found the homework prepared you for the exams very well and everything was clearly worded.

Dr. Beaulieu is an amazing professor. She's reasonable, encouraging, and caring. The textbook's required, there was extra readings and the assignments/tests were based strictly off the readings. Some content is a bit outdated, but most were quite applicable for the current era of Indigenous People in BC. I'm upset there was no mention of Slahal.

Dr. Rosario needs to be studied by other professors at WCU so they can learn exactly what to do. If Rosario offers a course for your major, TAKE IT!!! This is my second semester having him and I would not have survived 110 or 259 without him. Amazing lectures, resources, slides, demonstrations, and fun facts.

The class was unnecessarily difficult for only being an introduction course. The entire grade depends on the tests, which are much harder than the level she teaches you at. I am normally a very good student and I still barely passed her class. I do not recommend taking any of her courses unless you want to be quite frustrated the whole semester.

She's a very smart, sweet, and caring professor. She wants everyone to learn and enjoy doing it. You don't really have to read what is assigned, but she really pushes for participation and will dock points if you don't. You don't even have to go to class most days, she'll email everyone after every class.

Usually, professors don't take attendance into count because the first week classes begin, everyone is withdrawing from classes and whatnot. The test questions were all subjective trick questions and although the lectures and reading materials were interesting they didnt help. I even work in the same industry and it was like the twilightzone. Beware of this course with this professor...the bad reviews are accurate.

Her lectures are reading off the PowerPoint with no enthusiasm. Bad class engagement and doesnt have sympathy to students. The class is do able if you can learn everything yourself quickly. LAs are better explaining concepts than her so they will be the best way to understand material plus YouTube.

Professor Campos is honestly a great professor. His exams are based on the book & gives a review of the class before the exam and basically gives every question so we know exactly what to look for. She was a decent enough teacher but she can be a bit rude at times. She makes it a point to force participation in class (calls on people who specifically aren't raising their hands). No clear directions, doesn't answer questions well, and if you're not in class you won't always know what's on test as she will add things during lecture that aren't in the online notes. All I can say is read your book as much as you can and learn to google and you might pass.

I had him for SCE-300, which is a new class for Space Foundations. He was a good professor who knew a lot. The only thing is that sometimes the lecture was boring. But the projects really helped me to learn and were the only homework. Really fun elective class and I'm glad I took it.
Easy class, great extra class, no foul language

The class is straightforward attend class and complete the assignments. The professor does make it simple and clear to understand it. During the class, 99% of the time professor will be talking and explaining non-stop and will include his opinion about the topic with "life lessons". Overall is was a great experience.

Erica made my first college foreign language experience amazing! Do not give enough time to complete quizzes and exams and never gives study guides for midterms or final. I email him for extra practice question but never answered the email. I would never take a class with this professor.

Made it to my senior year without having to leave a bad review for a professor, but this professor did it for me. I've spent 25+ hours on this course weekly, 4.0 GPA.

Dr. Sawatsky is by far one of the best professors I have taken in my entire college career. Her lectures are great and she provides examples of how to apply what we learned in the classroom. Graded assignments have clear feedback and she is truly a great teacher!

can be disorganized on the lecture materials but otherwise cares about the class and the students.

Wish I got payed that much to read slides as fast as I can. It wouldnt be a problem if he didnt skip over all of the practice problems. Also for someone who doesnt do much teaching, he is the slowest grader in the department.
