When I ws in her class I felt like I was listening to a text book translator. Im sorry for all who have taken the class.

The labs are group-oriented. Didn't have much homework. Didn't come off as very compassionate. Very straight-forward. Labs were fun and engaging. Went outside for a lab but needed to bring our own supplies for other labs. He provides lots of supplies though. He is well respected. Tests are long, around 70-80 questions. MC and written questions.

He is an okay professor. kind of old school. he doesnt use D2L and likes papers to be turned in by hand. You will need to read the textbook to fully to good on test. He gives you all the notes and handouts you need. very little quizzes and papers are given. Dont sit in the front row because sometimes he spits while hes talking.

Mr. Adlington is an AMAZING teacher. He really cares about his students and seeing them succeed. He is very accessible outside of class. The tests are pretty hard but all of the material he goes over . Homework does not count for much so make sure you do well on the tests in order to pass.

Not as bad as the other reviews make her seem. She definitely makes you work for it. The problem with this class isnt her imo, its the workload and intensity for a class thats 100 level. Sometimes felt like a 300 level class. In the end, if you try hard, youll be fine. Dont put off taking this bc of the reviews, get it done.

She is a lovely professor! Her class is very work-heavy (especially the exams), but the content itself isn't difficult. She gives plenty of time (minimum 5 days) to complete assignments and at the very start of the semester, gives you all the exact dates things will be both assigned and due. Through and through, she seems like a lovely person!

The probs are: the amount of complicated homework and the prof accent. overcome accent & he is a joy to learn from. Will not reteach any trig or algebra info needed for certain lessons, but will use his free time to make sure you grasp the concepts taught. if you study quiz/ class probs / test review you can pass the test. chegg hw. weekly quizz.

Truly an exceptional professor, he cares for his students and efforts to ensure understanding of the concepts. I have gained a clear awareness of both my strengths and areas for improvement. This class was not only informative but also engaging. Additionally, TAs go above and beyond to provide thorough responses to our queries.

Professor Graham didnt convey course material well. Her teaching method is ineffective, she has a poor attitude. I dont believe I got a fair grade. Many of my classmates feel the same as myself. She needs to be replaced with someone who can actually teach.

She is really sweet and caring, but she doesn't seem to know a whole lot about what she's teaching. She makes her powerpoints at the very last minute, and doesn't understand or contradicts half of the info shes "teaching", and she just straight up reads everything off the powerpoint. You can access them on laulima so you can easily miss her class.

He is one of the BEST Prof's in the I.E Department. This professor truly wants every one to pass his courses with an A. As long as you come to class and participate you will get an A. We truly need more professors like this guy at this University!!!!
Dr. Linda is very smart and knows the material with great depth. The classes are heavily built around case studies and homework which at times can be pretty difficult.

Professor Keeler has the worst teaching style of any professor I've ever had. She took what could have been a very interesting and informative class and turned it into 50 minutes of reading monotone off a script. She only focuses on dates and legislation, and barely looks up from her script during the lecture. She does not post her slides either.

I don't believe Schiff deserves the criticism he gets. I found Schiff to be very straight forward and his lectures weren't the best but gave you a good idea of the concepts talked about during class. Beware of curveballs on tests, there is always at least one curveball on each test.

Very sad to say that I would not recommend taking this professor! This was basically a self taught course for myself, personally. Must spend countless hours reading the textbook in order to pass tests. Many questions on tests are only mentioned in the textbook and not in class. If you are taking other courses, do NOT take this class.
WORST TEACHER EVER!!!! these reviews are true she is very disrespectful. GBC you chose the wrong English teacher.

I have mixed feelings. She is a very nice person and respects all of her students. But I did not find that she explained things very well. She makes many errors while teaching although she's not scared to go back and correct herself. Her tests we're very straightforward if you attend class. She is also always willing to help outside of class.
Easy gen ed credit. Lots of extra credit. Almost no out of class work other than paper and seeing a couple plays.

Professor Xiong did a fantastic job teaching CS240. The course itself was fairly difficult but all information was outlined and explained in the slides well. Attending lectures was helpful since he stayed afterward to answer any questions and occationally gave hints as to what would we would expect to see on exams.
His teaching style was fairly average. Some concepts had to be explained multiple times. His grading was lenient, and there was not much coursework.

Her lectures reduce engaging the Bible from experiencing the revealed Word of God fulfilled in the person of Christ to a mere dry academic, situational study. Also, if you miss a class, you may substantially lower your grade (several pop quizzes/assignments). That being said, she is a brilliant scholar, a kind professor, and a clear lecturer.

Dr. Gatison is probably the worst professor I've ever had, she doesn't even teach the class. Her GSA's teach and grade. When I asked for more info, I was just referred to the syllabus - where there was not the info I was asking for. There was also quite a few inconsistencies within her syllabus. Beware: her exams are worth half of the class.

Dr. Miller is nice but she did not teach. The class consisted of textbook work. Weekly homework and quizzes. I emailed her several times and she said she was too busy to attend office hours. Her grading is like a game and is very confusing. Did not learn much in this class. Usually get out of class early though

Professor Hart was the best. He was very understanding of personal issues or other class assignments. As long as you read the chapters that he assigns, you will for sure pass the class. Show up to meetings and participate. Only 2 essays, super easy and about one or two assignments a week. Quizzes/Tests are simple, just be thought provoking.

I've never been the best at math and have always avoided it at all costs but Prof. Webb made this class enjoyable and easy to understand! He is super helpful and is willing to work with students outside of class. As long as you communicate with him he's very kind, understanding, and helpful! I would 100/10 recommend Prof. Webb to anyone!

Dan was incredible at explaining concepts and answering questions. His office hours are extremely helpful. He didn't host lecture this year but he is still well-versed in the content. Will offer really helpful shortcuts and methods. He is a very fast talker, though.

Dr. Prevatt's energy is enjoyable to be in class with. The most critical thing I can say is for PSY330 specifically, it is already a very difficult class and her coverage of the topic is pretty weak. She offers test corrections & online quizzes that you can take as many times as possible. I've heard her teaching style in other classes is easier.

This is a great course. Ms. Rosenfeld is very clear on what she expects from each presentation, shes very understanding especially if you dont nail it the first few times, she really cares about giving everyone a good public speaking experience. Very nice, definitely take this course.
Okay class and okay professor, just a lot of unnecessary busy work.

DO NOT TAKE HER. Rude over email. Reads directly off lecture slides in a monotone voice that puts half the class to sleep. Worst brightspace organization I have ever seen, and I have taken classes where the professors are 50-60+ years old and are not very good with technology. This class will take something from you.

I really got a kick out of Grant and found him to be an amusing professor. To be honest, just do all your assignments and try your best and he will give you a good grade. Very accessible and willing to help outside of class. Make sure to label everything correctly and turn in all assignments on time.
Incredibly messy and inconsiderate. Doesn't really teach anything but just throws concepts at you expecting you to learn them as you go. Doesn't really know what she's doing half the time.

Borkin is a very kind woman who wants her students to succeed. As long as you get over the hurdle of figuring out her confusing setups on Blackboard for where to find your work, you will be fine. Half the class is group work, though, so get ready to be talking and interacting with your classmates a lot.

I know Professor Trumbo has a lot of negative feedback here, but I liked him. He is definitely someone who is naturally good at data & such so it can be difficult if you weren't a math nut in high school or in general. Once you get it, you get it - but you definitely have to work for it. I definitely like him as a person as opposed to as a teacher.

In the beginning, Allen seemed as if his class was going to be the hardest class to take, but as time progressed, he became more and more lenient. I don't know if he personal problems around this time, but he doesn't really even grade your papers. He literally told the class that we could turn in a blank paper for the due date and turn it in later.

Matson is an okay professor. She teaches the easier concepts in 132. Despite this, the questions she puts on tests are SUPER LONG and detail heavy, so memorizing her fixations are key to acing exams. However, this doesn't erase the fact that Matson, despite her bubbly and high school teacher vibe, is a very passive aggressive professor. Not great.

Dr. Harvey is a very knowledgeable person and knows what she's talking about. She had to change the class layout due to COVID protocol, which has made the semester a bit easier, but also still hard at the same time. 8 tests, reading assignments every week, and papers/presentations. Hard to get to the point in the lecture, and long-winded tangents.

Sangmi was a variety of things and being a sweet and kind hearted person were a couple. However she was super slow, the lectures were lengthy, and her sassy commentary was contradicting. Things couldve been much simpler if she went into detail with her syllabus and took time to read over the things she sent out.
He doesn't offer help, teaches very fast, grumpy and mean. I thought it was going to be easy during the first week, but it took a turn for the worst. Horrible teaching and lack of clarity.

Professor Sepsis was a good professor and cared a lot about the topic he was teaching. I learned a lot, but the lectures started to get a bit boring after we had been sitting in class for so long. There aren't many assignments, so big things are graded rather than small things. Generally pretty good and lenient with attendance.
She's pretty good. I don't really mind the class, I just hate the labs.

Prof Nurse is truly a compassionate professor who cares about her students a lot which is rare these days. Shes very intelligent and accessible both outside the class and via her emails. Physics 2 is no walk in the park and dont except it to be but prof Nurse does an excellent job in teaching and reinforcing the material. Highly recommend.

Such an interesting, funny teacher. I actually like coming to class. She clearly cares for students and wants us to do well. Is always willing to help (even answers emails late at night). Weekly work is annoying but prepares us for bigger assignments and is an opportunity for more points. It is college, so it isn't easy, but totally doable.

HIGHLY recommend you do not choose Professor Riley for this course. Lectures are not engaging and he reads the slides word-for-word verbatim. Assigns quizzes that are extremely specific and expects you to be able to come up with in-depth research about random firms. Extremely frustrating, by far the worst professor at Carlson I've had thus far

Justin Goins is a solid instructor. He gives plenty of examples and code demos in lecture. His assignment descriptions are so thorough and exhaustive that I never had to guess what some functionality needs to do. Great instructor, definitely planning on taking as many courses with him as I can.

Prepare for a LOT of work between homeworks and recitations. The group project and final are 50% of your overall grade and are within the last three weeks of the semester. He crams 4 midterms into the first half of the semester to give time to focus on the project. One of the only classes where you'll learn excel and chemcad decently well.

Absolute worst Hunter has to offer. Don't listen to the previous reviews and trust me on this one. He gives so many papers(not the problem)but the way he grades them and the way he looks for specific things is ridiculous. Absolute ridiculous policies regarding attendance and talks about demonic stuff all the time. Don't take him. You will regret

You must teach yourself everything. Assignments graded ruthlessly for someone who speeds through lectures and rather than answering questions, points you toward the module. If that were sufficient, we wouldnt be asking. I dont pay thousands to teach myself everything.

Professor Izadi, is a very nice and caring person. Her accent is very understanding. But her class was very unorganized in many ways. Her group project assignments were so confusing and what she was asking for was so unclear. Her exams are a bit horrible because some of the questions made no sense. You have to ask a lot of questions to understand

Hope to god that you don't have to take UNIV100 in the first place. The course is set up as an extended orientation, which I feel is kind of pointless and redundant. As for Anzyl herself, she is a nice person. She is very accessible outside of class and gives some moderately good feedback. However, she is a tough grader, so be prepared for that.
Professor Diaz is caring and brings energy to her class. She gives one worksheet and one 20 question quiz per week. You have to use the book to complete these. She is flexible with hard assignments.

She was pretty good at teaching math, but she doesn't separate her personal life from her professional life very well; it's very obvious when she is in a bad or good mood, especially if you take a lot of retakes. She also tends to like people with better social skills, so if you're neurodivergent, keep interaction to a minimum.

Prof Hindes was very straight to the point. He had an organized way of explaining the subject which made it much more palatable. He's got a huge amount of math knowledge so sometimes he might go over your head but if you stop him he will explain. Participation is based off daily quizzes so show up and you can get extra credit.

Professor McGarr was very genuine and had clear passion for the subject, especially the history of journalism. We had 1 midterm, 1 final, 2 research essays, and various other activities. Discussion is mandatory! The material wasn't necessarily difficult, but it is a Comm B so it was a lot of work. Make sure to keep up and go to lecture!

In his class you have to do a simulation of a marketplace and it is so confusing and hard to understand. He is very passionate about it too and takes it very seriously so if you do bad on it... good luck passing the class. I had to spend so much money between that and the online textbook which i find crazy. Overall an Ok teacher.

I don't think the rest of the reviews here are fair. Overall, this instructor teaches a good class. The lectures compliment the rest of the material reasonably well. He takes the time to offer plenty of recorded lectures, videos, and reading. Do the work, & you'll do fine. Nice guy who gives good feedback. Not a bad professor at all.

Be prepared for a group project in this course. I think Dr. Starkey is a great professor, he's just not good at communication. I recommend you get the textbook for this course. He sometimes comes off kind of rude but overall I would recommend taking him for this course.

Prof allowed me to get back into enjoying creative writing, on many different topics. She does want constant participation, especially when talking on the readings. She is understanding and willing to accommodate to working with you outside of class time. Take her!
Saurez is an ok professor, but the class itself is awful. Do not take unless you have to. Extremely disorganized and just a terrible class

Had A LOT of audio issues w/ the hybrid online class at the beginning. You get an attendance grade so you need to show up. Gives out an untimed study guide "quiz" that is exactly what you will see on the tests. No lockdown browser. One big group project for the whole semester therefore multiple papers to be written, plus a presentation.

Honestly, Dr. Watt is such a nice person and has a great personality. However she is the MOST picky person I've ever experienced. She takes off points for very small things. If you don't breathe chem you'll have a hard time. For lab reports dont expect anything more than a B because she is so nit picky but doesn't clearly write out what she wants.

Mrs. Eskridge was very considerate and laid back. Is very serious about assignments and reminds students when they are due. Pay attention because she will ask questions. Sometimes her assignments can be misleading, however bring it up and she'll make sure it understandable. Other than that show up and do assignments its an easy A.

I hated this class so much. It's really useless and awful. Her grading criteria is so weird and random. Overall the class isn't that hard. Final is not proctored. Quizzes are easy, all answers on quizlet. Actual writing assignments are hard, You have to do 2 group projects, very annoying. Shes not super quick to respond either. Participation counts

Dr Checura teaches off of repetitive powerpoint slides word for word and we had 4 exams and one TA assignment and an extra credit assignment. She provides a ton of information but if you study her slides you should be able to get an A in the class.

Just like many other of my teachers, this teacher can be summarized like, "Great teacher, terrible grader." If you're trying to keep a GPA of 4.00, don't take the teacher. Others have also said, 95% of your grade is based SOLELY on 4 closed book exams with one attempt each. Also, there's no study material for the exams other than the lectures.

I wouldn't rec Zimet. Hypercritical and not in a productive way. She publicly shamed people in our class. Ironically she wasn't open to different learning styles. We had to go repeatedly to DRP so she'd allow recording for students with disabilities. Admittedly, my writing improved some, but it was an awful experience. Tenure is a heck of a drug.

He never shows up to class and constantly cancels class as well, when he shows up he's always late. He doesn't teach, he plays youtube videos that are 1-2hrs long and doesn't teach, his sense of humor is weird and he made me not like Graphic Design.
Tough Grader, had to learn everything outside of class.

This woman is unbelievably unorganized. She'll blame it on the past instructor but it's all her! She marks tough and chooses favourites (so suck up to her ego). She is very condescending/rude and expects more than what she gives. Her class is online/in-class so I basically taught myself. Thank god this class is over for me. Good luck you'll need it

Really sweet professor. She wants everyone to get engaged in class, and she tries hard. Tests are hard, not gonna lie. One in-person test for me before COVOID started and then the rest online. Will work with you if need be.

I had Professor Slagle for ENR2300 Society & Natural Resources. Being a sociology based course, I was afraid that I would be completely uninterested in the material. Professor Slagle made this the most enjoyable class of my semester! The lectures were engaging and her case studies were related to large, important topics within the environment.
Dr. Brinkley does an amazing job exlaining really complicated urban planning concepts - like California housing policy. She is funny- and makes learning fun. You will get to know your classmates too.

I took Prof Kodaverdian's class in Fall 2020. The class was very by the book and pretty boring, but her grading was straightforward and it was decently easy. A lot of lectures and weekly quizzes, but if you do all the readings, you should do well. Makes you write a paragraph write-up in addition to each reading, which was a lot of hw.

You just have to do well on all HW assignments. There are 9 and he drops the two lowest grades, which makes that 70%. And exceptionally well on the first midterm (30%) so you don't have to take the second midterm. He gives extra credit too! Take him!
Great teacher! Very kind, compassionate, and encouraging.

If I could rate this professor a zero, I would.
When I tell you this is by far the most UNREASONABLE teacher I've had so far... This teacher claims to want to help students, yet every time I did, they did not help at all. Tell me how you're supposed to be a wellness class when you don't even care about the wellness of your students?

Nice guy, you can tell he is a new professor due to his ability to get behind. The whole semester we were 2 weeks behind and when test came around he would have to combine units, for example, half of unit 1 and half of unit 2. He was always there to help if needed and gave up to 5 points of extra credit for the semester from attendance and quizzes.

Explains the assignments well. There are group projects and individual assignments for the class, but Prof. Smidt is more than willing to provide help. He also gives a generous amount of extra credit, so as long as you attempt extra credit and follow along in class, you are destined to get an A!

Good lecturer but lectures too much. Lost a lot of time to finish the labs. No lab works allowed outside of class. No time to be curious--MUST have prior knowledge of electronics. Gives short quizzes on assigned (several) chapter readings. Avoid this course if it's not required. You're screwed if it is required, HAHA!!

I was in the lab class; had a quiz, pre-lab and post-lab due every week. The professor was too disorganized for me and graded assignments late. But with just doing all my assignments and labs it's pretty easy to keep a good grade. You do have to read the lab before coming into class, but I would skim through it and have a good understanding.

Dr. Bowe REQUIRES proper citations in every aspect all the time. She is big on Tier 2 plagiarism, and she will provide you with examples of assignments that scored well, so use them! She gives you the template, and all you have to do is put your ideas in. She allows resubmissions, which is great, and she gives THOROUGH feedback. Super responsive.

AVOID. Grade is based on 3 exams, but exams are very tricky and complicated. Rushes through lectures when the content is too much so it's a hard time learning in class. He says there's a textbook but there is absolutely no correlation to the content taught in lecture. Nice guy but very unorganized and unnecessarily complicated class.
A lot of homework. You have to be in class or you will miss so much material. You go through a whole chapter a week. Take home quizzes and homework all the time. In class quizzes as well.

Not a super difficult class, but there is a decent amount of information to learn for quiz's and tests. I found the lectures to be mostly boring. Pay attention to the PowerPoint and fill in the blanks on the handout. As long as you study the lecture notes that he hands out each class you will be fine.

Definitely the worst prof Ive ever had. His lectures are really boring, his grading criteria is VERY unclear, and although he may come off as a nice person, I dont think he is tbh. If you have to take Anth 110, take it with literally ANY OTHER PROF!!!

If you are looking for a biology professor who makes you interested in the subject, do not take this class. Class is easy (online testing) but effort and materials to engage students was not very good. Bio has plenty of materials that help you learn outside the class, but if you are interested in a teacher who can teach well,look for someone else.

this class is tough, requires a lot of studying and hw prep, but dr. osborn is fun and explains grammar concepts well. does a good job at making spanish relevant to our building construction majors. she speaks only in spanish. I hated this at first but started getting it once I did the readings and visited her office hours (helps a ton!!)

I got prof Lennert by coincidence since I didn't know who would be teaching the class. Turned out amazing, he is really good at delivering everything you need to know to write a good paper in an entertaining manner.

Professor Long is good. She did not do anything that make me dislike her. I took her 8-week class and it was hard. Had about 10 assignments a week, which is ridicules. The assignments have no purpose and the test are actually hard, especially when you do not learn the material through notes or the assignments. Okay but not terrible. You can do it.

She's a terrible teacher! Her class is basically reading the textbook out loud. She is just so bad at explaining things. The grades of this class also come out really late. Now it's way pass final grades due and it seems like she just started grading.

This class if very homework heavy, one chapter every week, but it does help your grade and it's easy to get 100 on the homework. Biggest downfall is that the homework is nothing like the tests. The tests are very hard and I don't feel we're fully prepared for them. He does drop the lowest test grade which helps tremendously.

Took this class as a GE. Super easy and clear tests, multiple choice. The professor kind of just reads off the slides in class. Teaching quality wasn't amazing, but the difficulty and tests were very easy.

Great professor and was a really good class time for his 10am to 10:50am class Monday through Thursday, he explained course material very well and was very interactive. If you need a great explanation of things he will give it to you.

Lectures are boring & confusing, they also don't correlate with the assignments. He didn't start grading work until 2 weeks before the end of the semester and he grades really weird with little to no feedback. I did however pass with flying colors, there are no tests or quizzes, just 2 assignments a week and you can correct anything up to a 100.

Very laid back guy. He explains concepts to the point where you think you understand them until you get to the lab and are completely lost. Lecture did not focus on coding as much as I would have liked. Tests are not particularly hard, but there is no partial credit. He does give a ton of drop grades, though.

Tough grader, and for all large assignments you have to click back and forth between instruction sheets, rubrics, and her emails to know exactly what you need to include for full credit. This is confusing and a waste of time. Even then, she docks points for leaving out things that weren't even mentioned in her emails, instructions, or rubrics.

I took this class in a 6 week summer session, it was literally so easy. She is super fun, super understanding and she clearly just didn't wanna seen anyone fail. I still learned from the course but there were no class meetings just lectures posted and purely discussion forums. Responded to 2 questions per week and responded to 2 other student's.

Mr. Scott is a really chill and funny professor. Test, projects, and assignments are all on SAM. Very lenient on due dates and is very cooperative. Encourages group work and wants you to be engaged and participate in class! Great professor overall!!
he is very strict and a lot of quizzes and exams

at first, professor Richie was very helpful but midway through the course (the hardest part) she stopped answering my emails, would just post powerpoints of the lecture and some youtube teaching videos. there are 5 essays, 4 projects, and discussion posts. The assignments are pretty tedious and require a lot of work. she takes a long time to grade

One of the easiest classes I have taken at this University. A lot of critical thinking and analyzing, even if it isn't your best work, as long as you turn something in ON TIME, you will pass the class. If you have trouble, reach out, she is very understanding and kind. Easy grader, wants everyone to succeed! highly recommend!!! A million stars!!

No matter how hard I tried, I could not obtain a plain A. When asked for feedback, she said there were too many grammatical errors to enumerate. When pressed for an example, the "error" she pointed out was not an error at all! It was grammatically correct! She is also too subjective and may not be the best person to teach undergrad courses.
Doesnt help you if you ask questions. Wont help if you miss a class and try to make it up. Not caring at all. Doesnt try and understand your situation. Likes to fail students more than to pass them.

Uhm, Ms. Rodriguez was very strict for a college professor. Attendance is mandatory. She knew her material, went fast, and was really strict. As long as you do her papers, do good on her tests, you should get an A; however, she is really strict in the classroom.

The attendance policy made no sense and her running the whole class time but hardly showing us how to do the problems was literal torture. Mymathlab literally takes hours per assignment waste of time for useless class.

Listen to me - Professor Nguyen is the guy to take if you want an A. He explains concepts clearly. Yes, there is math involved but he explains things so you understand. He knows that some concepts are difficult and he tries to explain things so all can understand, even the math-challenged, like myself. TAKE HIM!! You won't regret it!

Very engaged in the class. Tries to make the class as fun as it can be and tries to keep the class entertained through videos and dancing. Allows and encourages us to express our opinions and thoughts on a dance. Humorous and caring.

I learned a lot through group discussions and the book, her intentions are good, you can tell she cares about the topics we discuss, her quizzes are 1 min 25 sec per question. If you do bad or average in the quizzes it will reflect drastically in your grade. 3 papers, 1 group project. If your taking more than four classes it can be difficult.

If you don't mind showing up to class here and there and speaking, Vicki's class is for you. I showed up for about half of the classes but was sure to chime in here and there, she was respectful and the class was actually fun. I learned a lot and it's not useless information either. So its a win-win. Ideally what a uni class is supposed to be.

This is a difficult class! She does teach this class harder than other professors. With that said it is passable and you will learn a lot. She is more than willing to help out if you put the time in. Great professor if you put in effort.

Minimal requirements, if youve taken him you know what i mean. If your paper is lacking something from wrong font size to wrong header, no page number, messed up citations, or anything like that you get a 0. He doesnt even read the paper its just a 0. And the papers are worth like 25% of your grade so if you mess up 2 papers its over.

This class will test your ability to comprehend information in a different way. I had no programming experience going into this class which probably made it a lot harder, but Professor Lieberman is GREAT at explaining the syntax, as well as the grading criteria. Highly suggest taking him, but maybe after taking Python or Java first.

No insult to GB, she is a perfectly fine person. She's very polite and wants to get to know her students. This being said, we are in the last few weeks of the class, and the papers that we have turned in so far have still not been graded. I have absolutely no idea how I am doing in this class. The discussions in this class are dull as well.

Very passionate about the class but he moves through the PowerPoint way too quickly, and I never had enough time to write it all down or even take a pic of the slides sometimes. Tests are very in depth, more so than he covers in class. I know people who dropped it part way into the semester. Doable, but I do not recommend.

If you like philosophy you will love her, if you don't you will not. She makes you work for it. You have to read a lot, then understand, then apply it to the questions on the quizzes. She had a good mix between quizzes and written papers. Save/type every quiz question and answer!!!! The exams are the same questions as the quizzes!

Yener is a funny guy and wants you to succeed. Go to his office hours for anything you're not sure on. The lab practice tests are the exams just some are reworded. Study the lab book and you'll do fine. He will catch you copying homework so be careful. Pick your seat the first day careful, that determines your group for the rest of the semester.

Terrible teacher. Online quizzes are near impossible, goes through PowerPoint WAY too quick, and doesnt post notes. He preaches that we should protest and not peacefully, brought in a speaker to say so as well. Hes just not a helpful and inspirational professor. I withdrew and I needed the class. Thats how bad it was.

I recommend this course and Dr. Nopper is an excellent communicator. Expect to learn taking this course, no coasting. If you follow her rubric and read her weekly feedback you will have the tools to be successful. The material is relevant. For once in a long while I did not feel ripped off paying the PSU high tuition course credit.

Malena (her preferred name) is awesome! Her class was always so much fun, as she finds ways to teach lessons by playing fun games. She's very honest, gives good feedback and tips, and is just hilarious. You can tell she cares about her students and wants them to succeed. Take her if you have the chance!

Dude was rude and took so much time to return assignments. I got a B but I felt like his presence was unnecessary. I pretty much taught myself. Avoid at all costs
Textbook is required, doesnt not allow resubmission for tests past due date

Dr. Bolyard is a wonderful human and passionate about her job. I felt like I was being treated like a kid instead of being trained to teach kids. The lesson plan assigned were long and detailed and there are a lot of group projects and silly games.

Lectures can be a little slow. It's better if you review the readings before class. There was a term paper as a final. That was the only difficult assignment in this class. Dr. Shortt is very flexible when it comes to late work. Great guy!

This class was great. Prof Toler is really into horror and pop culture so everything in the class reflects that. Probably one of the easiest classes I have ever taken. He is very understanding and funny. I plan on taking ENG201 with him again.

The lectures themselves are very boring, he is a good professor and is interesting, the material is just super boring. Gets points for attendance which are important. There is a lot of quizzes and reading, but the quizzes are on computer so you can look at study guide. Tests are difficult. He does have an accent but pretty easy to understand.

I LOVE Professor S. Had her for both Chem102 Lecture & Lab. Goes very fast but very knowledgeable and cares about her students. Very helpful in lab but can come off as snappy at times. Tests are very fair to what was learned in class and are very similar to practice tests. Just make sure to turn in your work on time! I 100% recommend her!
This class was one of the hardest GE classes I have ever had. You have to watch every single lecture and take careful notes. I do not recommend her class at all!

I really really enjoyed Dr G.'s class. I couldn't recommend him more. The class does require some effort (there are lots of readings and a decent amount of papers) but I found that Dr. G does his very best to set you up for success. I also felt that he genuinely cared about his students and their success both in his class and in life.

This class is not statistics, it's coding. Only take if you really want to learn Rstudio. Professor Odell is a very dry lecturer and assigns problem sets that are way too hard for people who are just trying to fill their math requirements. During office hours, he is not helpful and very condescending. I spent hours on the problem sets.

I took this class online, so it was a little different. She gave us extra credit on all 5 exams just by completing a kahoot. Homework was hard but doable, and discussions were fine. The cheat sheet for exams helped me a lot. I'm not sure if I would've done well without the sheet. I'd recommend introducing yourself to her to make a connection.

He gives very vague instructions then grades you on this elaborate rubric that he created without informing the students. He takes at least half credit off of almost everything. AVOID TAKING HIS CLASS AT ALL COSTS!!!!!

Joe is a great person, very understanding and kind. However, his teaching style is not helpful at all. The class average for every test we had was below 62%, and for the final paper he stated that he felt guilty that people did so well. He purposely made material confusing and hard so you could use critical thinking. Wouldnt recommend:(

His lectures are literally him speed reading slides and they will put you to sleep. Do the homework intensely and study every single week outside of class because he will only confuse you when you are trying to learn the concepts

He's a really solid professor. His office hours are really helpful if you're struggling. His hand writing does suck but he'll clear up anything if you ask. He's really nice and willing to help anyone who's struggling.

Dr. Mishra is an awesome professor! He is so knowledgeable, empathetic and supportive. You can tell that he really wants his students to be successful. He has a great lecture style and knows so much about every topic! He always responds to emails and questions, and goes the extra mile to help you.
Didn't want to help the students achieve and never gave feedback. Also refused to meet with me over zoom to help

Dr. Rojas was great! Gave examples and thoroughly explained everything we learned! Power points were also posted in D2L which was helpful. Exams were online but I'd still study! The one book you have to read is the best book ever. He's very genuine and nice and understands if you aren't able to make it to class. I'd recommend his class to anyone!

Armen is a good professor but the homework and lab assignments are insanely hard and take hours to complete. He is helpful if you need help on any assignments but you will spend a ton of time outside of the class doing assignments. Tests are somewhat easy and is pretty much straight from lectures.

Nice guy, not a great prof. For an intro lab class, he introduces concepts and mathematics in lecture way too advanced, so you never really understand them, but the actual labs are infantile. If youre a creative writing minor or English major, just know that shes very clear that you are. You are graded by final portfolio as well as attendance. If youre a person who cant get to class on time, remember that she will point you out in front of the entire class because youre late. She will keep talking about latenesses.

Decent class, the work is fairly easy. One group project, make sure you contact your partner EARLY because the class is online, so group projects were quite difficult to manage. It was also very difficult to get a response from the teacher, sometimes 2-3 days. I will say I did indeed learn in this class, but it could've been a better experience.

This class was a joke and a waste of time. Leisner doesnt do anything and just relies on the TA's to grade everything. Unfortunately the TAs my class had were insanely harsh graders and it was impossible to make an A on the tests with extremely vague short answer questions. I learned absolutely nothing in this class but still somehow got an A.
She is awesome and very helpful, use her as a resource for help!

Nice but unclear with assignments & gives a lot of work. Expected to read articles and submit a 2 pg paper on fieldwork observations before every class. Class is discussion lead by her for the full two hours. You are required 20 hours of fieldwork in total, so leave time in your schedule for that. Final is an 8 pg paper, presentation, & photobook
Worst teacher at UofW. Could not make out a word he said. Stay away if you're trying to learn accounting.

Professor Bechtold is truly one of the best professors at WPU. His class gives you a real understanding of studio lighting & you can tell he clearly loves what he does. Each week he teaches you the lighting set up and never keeps you till 10:30. His class was so good I took it twice. Genuinely a real good dude with a passion for photography - 10/10
Good Luck.

The everyday discussion gets pretty boring, but the paper prompts are very confusing. He asks a million questions in them and then takes off points if you don't answer a question he didn't ask in the prompt. I don't think his grading was very fair, considering that the only grades are 3 papers.

Dr. George is hands down one of the best math professors I've ever had. She's really caring and understanding. Her lectures are wonderful. Her notes are very valuable. Homework is usually heavy and takes a long time to get through but that's just to push us to become better mathematicians and coders. Can't overstate my recommendation! Take her.

Everything's super easy there's 3 papers throughout the whole term and he literally emails you the corrections he wants you to make. But attendance is mandatory and if you don't show up good luck. He's also boring so class was tough for me.

Brother Marrot is arrogant and intentionally vague in his lectures. His exams are very loosely related to his lecture and said we did not have to worry about studying certain things that actually were on the test. He did this throughout the semester. I was shocked at his good reviews, I felt like I was set up to fail.

Udd should not be a professor. He will literally waste your time and his classes are a waste of money. He goes off on tangents about his personal life and complains about his mother in law. He distracts himself from teaching. He will openly assume things about you, tell you, and not let you change his mind if he is wrong. Wish I could rate him zero

Grades are well split, you have participation grade (attendance), weekly reading quizzes (very easy and good way to bump up your grade), 3 HW assignments and 3 midterms. He is a very caring professor, very clear, well planned lectures and he answers emails super quick and is very understanding.

If you need to take Brink for an online class get ready to get the most difficult and outdated teaching style you've ever seen. He gives three page long instructions for an essay, and will only reply through email, but only if you meet the right criteria in the email. He is probably the toughest grader I've ever encountered. Take someone else.

Professor Tyson is a really caring person. However I never liked his class because we had lots of homework that I could barely understand. He also goes really fast with his lectures so make sure you take advantage of office hours. Overall if you want to do well in this class do your homework on time, ask questions and do extra practice on your own.

I would not take anything offered by this professor again. This was by far the least organized course of the program for me. The lecture videos continued errors, the exams were often quite hard, the readings were not engaging, and I found the assignments to be busy work. I also found the content to be a repeat of several other courses.
Very hard grader but food instructor

You can also look her up at Uni of Massachusetts. The class is all lecture, and the tests are short answer. She is very knowledgeable, but bombards with information. She does place the slides online and if you take really good notes to fill in missing info not on slides that she lectures on, you just may pass the tests. Its not an easy class

I really didn't love this class. It has way too much reading & there are essays every other week that you have to write. Sister Spear is a decent teacher. She wasn't always very clear about certain things, like citing properly in your essays. But, she tells you at the beginning of each week what is due that week, so there's no misunderstandings.

Kimberly Chiew was a very smart professor however her lectures were mind-numbing. I probably went to 4 of the classes during the entire quarter, just didn't have the energy to sit through those lectures ever. There are no assignments to keep you engaged in the topics and pretty much everything is based on the exams.

Assignments were fairly easy and straightforward. For quizzes, we were unable to move back to review or change our answers; which was quite annoying. After you got marks back from quizzes you could only see what you got wrong by having a meeting with the prof. The prof was nice and provided good feedback, but wouldn't take a class with them again.
Walters is a alright teacher but he talks way too much. His lectures are important for the tests but they are very boring. He grades reasonably but if you want credit you have to earn it.

Quizzes every week. Mandatory attendance. The projects are super difficult because he doesn't explain it until AFTER the due date. Try to take another professor if you could. His projects are super stressful.

Dr. Moskalik is good at the material she teaches, but needs to work on teaching it. Lectures are dense and lacking engagement. Sometimes there's group work to accompany lecture, but it's rare. Readings are dense and you'll struggle in class if you don't do them. The class is meant to be "hybrid" after week 6, but it is really just extra work.
so inspirational, really makes people think about writing and what they're writing about. a great grader, super caring, really cares about her students and the things she teaches.

This guy understands the material well but is absolutely horrendous at teaching it. He doesn' explain anything and if you miss one thing in class, good luck because you'l never learn it again. No lecture videos, no slides for explanation. Interesting class but Jamie is never accessible and honestly that's the only thing that makes this class hard.

I am currently enrolled in this class and it is arguably the most difficult class I have taken and I am an honor student. The assignments aren't bad at all, but the quizzes are extremely difficult. This class makes me cry because I know my GPA is about to drop over this class :')

There's a lot to like. He made contacting him about anything really easy. He was accessible most hours of the day. Pushed back deadlines if he felt necessary, that was very much appreciated. I did find, however, he often went off on rants. He also seemed to love to reminisce about his past during these rants. That irked me a little.
He doesn't have a clear grading rubric so it was super hard to vision what he wants in quizzes or tests. There was a lot of lectures and all of them are boring.

David is a nice guy but he is kind of a tough grader. He sometimes looks for very very specific things in the assignments or quizzes. If you want an A then I would recommend someone else instead of him. It is very hard to get an A in his lab.

Every week we had to read about 30-50 pages of the textbook and take a quiz. There were two exams which covered very knit-picky details from the textbook so you had to take very good notes and study well to do okay. Professor was available. Wasn't prepared to have to do so much work for a class outside of my major.
Good at facilitating interesting group discussion and gives useful feedback.

Great professor! This special topics class was abnormal child psychology; it was about childhood behavior disorders. Professor Lansing was always very enthusiastic & willing to offer help to students. Easy class. Few # of quizzes and tests - could take them online at home. Attendance was randomly taken - had to answer a question she posted in class

I really enjoyed having Sandra as a teacher. She likes those who participate, and come prepared for class. It really didn't take much to do well in this course. I just skimmed through the assigned readings, specifically the bolded words in the textbook in order to prepare for the weekly quizzes.

Kristie is a great professor, and her passion for the subjects she teaches really shows in her teaching style. Kristie cares about students and gives great feedback on papers and projects. Reading discussions are helpful so I suggest actually doing the readings. She also takes students opinions and recommendations into consideration.
Great detailed caring professor. He makes you read and participate but you will learn a lot in his classes. Full of real world information.

Dr. Wallace is a good guy, and takes the time to try and get to know his students. However, his class was often repetitive and it feels like our actual course content was rarely touched on, as Dr. Wallace likes to talk about his work experience and the same 3-4 stories and tries to relate it to the class. Very tough grader, not very clear rubrics.

Pretty chill professor. You do need to go to class to understand what's happening. He does record the lecture and uploads it later. You get weekly homework, classwork, and quizzes. But as long as you do those and the final project you should be fine.

My experience with Dr. Duffy was awful. I wish I never wouldve enrolled. She gets frustrated easily and lashes out. Also, for both concerts we had she didnt pick which pieces we were doing until the week before and then was angry when they werent perfect. Practices felt disorganized and stressful. Wouldnt recommend.

Really great teacher who actually made me look forward to algebra for the first time. Hes very funny and great at explaining things. He does have a lot of homework though, and occasional pop quizzes. Textbook isnt required but you need to pay to be able to do the HW!

The epitome of #teamtoomuch. While I appreciate him teaching professional game design practices, and the material was interesting, there were just too many assignments. Some weeks, we'd have an individual assignment, a team assignment, and a reading in 1 week, just to spend too long playtesting. I would only take if you want to go into game design.

Professor Carneglia is super awesome. I love her class, and currently have a 100%. She is really good at teaching and her canvas course is laid out really well. I have really enjoyed her class so far, and I'm so glad I got her as a professor.

This professor is not good. Especially for online classes, she is the most unorganized professor. Gets back to you pretty fast but is not clear AT ALL. You have a mandatory visit to the Dallas Museum Of Art, it is so boring. The class was a complete waste of time, only took it because it was one of the election options. Tests are ridiculous.

Probably the BEST professor I've had at UAF. He's amazing, and was very understanding when I fell behind in class due to a family emergency. He's very down to earth and easy to get a hold of if you need him. Love this dude I ALWAYS recommend him!
Super awesome Professor. Really easy going and very helpful when you have questions.

Shes a nice woman but a horrible teacher. She assigned so much homework that I gave up on it, as i took this as a high school senior with five other college/AP courses and I only needed a C to keep my GPA intact due to the weights at my hs. Shes an amazingly nice woman but is hard to understand, expects too much, and doesnt know how to teach.

The class itself is not hard, but the professor is w/ grading wise. She doesnt guide us well on how to do certain assignments. You have to figure it out how exactly you want to do it. Like others said, she is a tough grader. She grades rather in a subjective manner than simply sticking to the rubric. Unfair for students who are trying their best.

As a professor and a nurse, Prof. Misir is knowledgeable, dedicated, respectful, comforting, and wants the best for others. She works hard to make sure we get the most out of our clinical experience without making you anxious. She has truly inspired me to be the best nurse I can be and gave me the tools to do so. Hope I can take her again!

My classmates and I had an unusual experience with 4 instructors teaching our class.  While it was challenging having so many instructors, I don't regret taking the class. Elizabeth stayed behind after class or Zoom meetings to answer questions. She provided timely feedback and held review sessions before exams. I enjoyed her teaching style.
The assignments weren't very good at relating to English. this is a class for people who have never taken any English.

Dr. Qu does not pace the class well, so you're left with a lot of very hard content crammed at the end. It is almost impossible to keep up with the class, and as a result of his time management, he is unable to take questions on the most difficult material. The only redeeming qualities are that he recorded the lectures and dropped the lowest exam.
Ridiculous class--it was so hard. But the professor is very accessible and helps you out if you ask him for it.

Mr. Kafley is a great professor and an awesome lecturer. Just attend his class and take the lecture notes. The homework, quizzes, and tests are based on his lecture notes. Math- 150 is not an easy class, you have to spend a lot of time working on homework assignments. Make sure that you learn to factor quadratic on your own before you start Unit 2.

Jimmy is one of the best professors I've had. He really cares about his job and wants to help his students as best as he can. He goes above and beyond what is necessary of himself to make sure that every student who wants help gets it. Everyone I've spoken to loves him as a professor and loves the laid back atmosphere he fosters in class.

Expects extremely detailed work for very simple problems (such as showing work for a 3-4-5 triangle), will not award partial credit and will not explain examples clearly in class. Very hard to understand and only answers questions with "yes" "no" and "I don't know." May show up to office hours, may not, it's a gamble. Be prepared to teach yourself
Not recommended, unfair grading, not available for students

4 exams and 4 pop quizzes are your only grades throughout the semester. Highly recommend learning the slides very well because his test questions are directly from his slides. Be aware that he springs several pop quizzes on you throughout the semester. No grade replacement of dropped quizzes/exams.

Professor Alsup is everything you could ask for in a teacher. She is caring, gives great feedback, and genuinely cares about you. She is understanding of personal situations and gives great feedback. Even online, her class is engaging and challenges you, but still fun and easy to pass because the expectations are clear. I would take her if you can!

I had about 3 classes all semester because she canceled them all and even the ones we had were either 20 mins long or started 20 mins late. The grading system was messed up and I still dont know what I have. The work we had didnt pertain to the lectures. I would stay far away if you want your mental state to stay intact.

Lectures were long and boring. Weekly "conference" with TA is really helpful, attendance for credit with TA! Honestly you don't have to go to the lectures if you go to the conferences! A LOT of work! weekly assignments that mess with your mind. I did learn how to write a better essay and research process but i don't know if it was worth it.
If you miss any class points immediately are taken off, otherwise a good professor, but I don't like the lack of flexibility.

Get your bibles out because you'll be using them. I recommend you download the app bible gateway. Make sure to read the articles and bible readings for the daily quizzes. Landfair is passionate about the bible but there is too much participation and the essays are confusing. As long as you try your best to participate and read you should be good.
Hard to understand his accent. Im Mexican and still couldnt understand what he was saying 60% of the time

If you like a challenge, then Holloway is the professor for you. His exams are tough but entirely doable. However his lectures are a bit disorganized, and he doesn't go over exam problems which would greatly increase our understanding if he did. If you do your homework and seek help from tutors if you're stuck then you should be fine.
I took this class in the summer online and it went by like a breeze. Never got to meet him in person but he seemed like a chill professor. I recommend you take this class!

Horrible experience, very unorganized. During lecture she hardly teaches anything. Its more of a teach yourself class. Has a sarcastic voice when shes going to humiliate a student for asking a question. Discourages students alot. Least helpful professors in the nursing program. Made it 10x harder.
Accounting is a hard topic to learn if you have never encountered it as I have. Prof Cikurel does a good job of teaching the subject. You will not go wrong with choosing him for ACC 101.
The teaching wasn't teaching enough.

This was her first semester teaching the class so she didn't have a well developed course. She gives two tests the entire semester. A midterm and a final. Other than that you have a quiz before every class to see if you did the required reading leading up to the lab.

Professor Rothstein is a great professor. The class is tough but very fair. She was very helpful with any questions I had. The "guided" notes we took in class on the material were VERY helpful as opposed to just copying what the professor wrote on the whiteboard.

I am BSN nursing student at Keiser University-Lakeland. I came with lot of fear about chemistry pre-req course. But after attending Dr. Raj Appavu's first class/lecture.. my fear has gone. He is very very helpful. You will 100% pass in chem2045 without any difficulties. Best wishes to new students
She provides powerpoints for each chapter and then just records herself going over the powerpoints as "lecture", very repetitive. Just read the chapters and powerpoints and you'll be fine.

Class lectures go over the same general ideas over and over again, lectures and discussions are void of any substance, and assignments are vague while being graded severely. Going to office hours doesn't help at all. 

After talking with the rest of the class it's clear that pretty much everyone feels the same way. 

0/10

Mrs. Zimmerman is one of the very good teachers that you will have in math. You do your homework and study you will pass her class. Ask a lot of question in her class so she can get to know your face. Make sure you get that access code or you will not pass the class.

For NEUROSCIENCE: Dr. Han can be unclear about what she expects from you & test directions arent always clear which can be frustrating ("select all that apply" applied to the entire test, but only 5/35 questions had multiple answers). Her Lecturing is fine, but you definitely need to read the book too. She respects and cares about the students tho.

This class is a little harder in the beginning but gets better. Her way of grading the class gives lots of opportunities to succeed in different kinds of work. She solicits and responds to student feedback on the class and is a really good lecturer.
Show up, talk, get an A.

This class is the most frustrating one Ive ever taken. While Professor Steelman is a nice woman and easy grader, there is loads of work and attendance is mandatory. She rarely comes to class prepared and gives a lot of busy work. Although, I got an A, I had to work for it.
The class is very long and there's a lot of material. Plays many instruments but the workload is a lot (quiz, written assignments, long midterm, concert reaction, oral presentation).

We used an online class for a class that had to be attended in person. The lectures often consisted of videos we would watch for the hour long and twenty minute class. Nice professor and always there to help the students. He can get quite loud during the lectures. His class is an easy A if you do the work and pay attention.

Put in minimal effort and you will receive full credit on everything. This course had 4 article reviews (just stating what the article said), a midterm, autobiography paper, a project, and another final project that counted as the final exam. Lots of papers, but do them and you'll get a 100. Gives lots of extra points too. Easy professor.

Andrew Hill is the worst professor I have had at Montana State. He is unwilling to help anyone, even if they make an appointment with him. Lectures are verbatim what is in the textbook and not engaging at all. For anyone who cannot teach themself or invest in tutoring, do not take this class with this professor.

Overall he is a good professor and organized. His class was not too difficult. He allows notes for midterm&final which are useful. He is very clear on what will be on the exams so just do as he says. I would take again. Overall pretty clear and no ambiguity. He is a phd student himself but overall good professor and very clear expectations.

The quizzes are online. He expects you to participate in class. If you do the work you will pass. Hes flexible on due dates, but strict about attendance. The lectures are informative. He has many stories.

She expects the students to memorize everything in a short amount of time. The lockdown browser is used on every quiz. The study guides she provides are NOT helpful for the quizzes/tests. I spent 9+ hours a week studying and didn't have a good outcome in my overall grade and I was above average in the class, sadly.

She is a sweetheart. She cares a lot about her students and will do anything to help you inside and outside of class. She is very passionate about the course she teaches and understanding of the fact that her class is an elective. Would take again DEFINITELY!

His class readings are inspiring. However, they are contrasted by the zero-tolerance grading policy. If you miss one of the requirements for an assignment you will get a zero. If you forget even one discussion board reply, you get a zero. No partial credit. He encourages you to drop. Example of what grading policy not to have as a teacher.

Professor Bucknum was a joy to have. His teaching style and demeanor was laid back and the atmosphere of the class was always chill and light. He is a genius when it comes to creative writing and I learned so much from him. I definitely recommend this professor to any and all students who have a love for creative writing. Enjoy!

This course is organized well and although the content is upper level the workload is not overbearing because it is well spaced. The professor provides detailed personalized feedback on every assignment, and is considerate of students. Expectations are well defined for all assignments.

Dr Ellis is extremely nice and if you are looking for an easy class this is it. If you are actually interested in Criminal Justice and want a professor who can provide first person examples and can answer questions outside of the text take this course with someone else.

Prof Weidenfeld uses some unconventional but highly entertaining methods in some of his courses, including a complicated role-playing historical simulation in this course. The latter half of the class was some of the most fun I've ever had in college, and his encouragement of engagement and questions in the lecture half was great. Would recommend.

Lots of reading and weekly quizzes. Lectures are quite long with a listening quiz after every class. If you miss one class your participation grade will drop drastically. There are two concert reports in her class which she does not offer an online option for. Very strict about grammar and spelling even though it is not an English class.

Cami is a fantastic professor, and her years of experience teaching and writing IEPs, make her a perfect match for this class.  She gives excellent feedback and makes sure you understand each section of the IEP before moving on to the next.  This class does have a lot of homework, but it never felt like "busy work" and was always relevant.
I great professor, would take him anyday. You won't regret having him.
This is the second course I've had with Professor Jurkowski. His classes are very easy and he wants you to succeed. I recommend his courses for GEs, even if the lectures can be boring at times.

Took this during COVID. Online synchronous - two lectures per week, hw due each week, 2 quizzes, 2 exams (midterm, final). He's a good teacher, and is kind, and doesn't care how many questions students ask, and makes sure they understand what they're confused with. TA graded harshly on homework so that's the only thing I didn't like.

The class could be taken in person or on zoom, after attending one in-person class I decided to just do zoom. All of the work is done on McGraw hill and the computer grades most if not all of your work. She seems very nice but overall I haven't really learned anything from her, most of the class is very independent work that is all graded online

Dr. Cravens is an excellent professor. She is very funny and very patient if you ask her for help, and will continue to guide you towards your solution until you understand it rather than just giving it to you. I would definitely take a class with her again.

She is very good if you are smart she will make you excel. But if you are looking for an ez A this is not the class. She teaches a more advanced class so you will learn more and actually be able to use the material out of the classroom.

I wish I had checked RMP prior to choosing this professor. Grading is unclear, specifically the discussion posts. A weird, hard to maneuver online book used. She sends out the same long email day after day, only the date changes.

He's clearly very knowledgeable. He does get off topic a lot, but he's funny and explains things well. There is so much content, but A+P is difficult by nature. The practicals are ridiculously difficult and near impossible. The lecture exams are 50 Q's in 50 mins which is so stressful. IDK. Not my favorite class. He has a bit of an ego I think.

Lectures were often confusing and seemed poorly prepared. Show up to class, and the tests are not take home. A lot of the examples were confusing and difficult to follow. If you show up and study you will get an A or B, but if you don't then don't expect a high grade. Put in the work required for this class if you want to do well.

He is an excellent teacher who knows what he is talking about. He does have multiple quizzes over his lectures, but you will know when the next quiz is. You will do a business simulation that is quite cool once you get the hang of it. You will spend more time on this than anything because you will do single player and a group against other groups.

Although some of the assignments were difficult, I found the course too be stimulating nonetheless. Prof Goyette is a very kind person, she shows that she cares about her students success and she seems passionate about the subjects. I can tell she puts a lot of time and effort in her course. I recommend but be ready for a high homework load.

Pro: Detailed notes and explanations
Con: REALLY fast paced lectures going from point to point without much time to ask questions

Note: She has an accent (Not too bad in my honest opinion)

If you're good with taking notes and have fast comprehension, you'll be fine. Otherwise you might struggle a bit.

Prof. Felten is uper chill! He's super nice and as long as you're not distracting others in class, you're cool. The syllabus does say attendance is mandatory but a few weeks in he stops taking attendance. His lectures are pretty easy and the work isn't due until the last day of the semester, so no pressure. No midterm or final, just online quizzes.

She cares about her students and wants to make connections with them. Half of this class consists of group projects where one assignment is submitted and the entire group shares the grade. There are no exams or in-class quizzes. Her grading is too harsh for a gen-ed requirement. She is not very receptive to opinions opposing her own.

Extremely rude to students and is not good at explaining things. The workload is absolutely insane, and that's coming from someone who took AP/IB classes in high school. There are essays about every week and there are frequently projects due. She is not very helpful when emailing her or asking about late work and comes across as cold.

His teaching style confused me since he didn't have slides and wrote stuff on paper in lectures, might be appealing to some but not for me. However, textbook and CSMC helped me understand the content. 2 tests worth 90% but very easy as long as you do the review quizzes beforehand.
